title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Take DIV/REM off the 200ns EX path: iterative radix-2 divider + single shared 33x33 multiplier
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz; the worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) is
clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex, i.e. the forwarding mux
feeding the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` operators in alu.sv
(four 32-stage array dividers: signed/unsigned x quotient/remainder).
Every instruction pays for that path every cycle, yet CoreMark's timed
region executes almost no divides (list/matrix/state/crc kernels are
add/shift/mul/load/branch). The ALU also elaborates THREE separate
32x32->64 multipliers (mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su), tripling DSP/LUT use
and widening the result mux. Removing the divider from the single-cycle
path is the single biggest lever available.
MEASURED (hypgen probe, Gowin `make timing`, place_option 0): replacing
the four DIV/REM arms with `a ^ b` (everything else untouched) gives
Fmax 46.49 MHz (vs 5.44), logic 2110 (vs ~12300 LUT4), DSP 6. The new
worst path (26.8 ns, 21 levels, 45 cells) is
u_rf -> u_id -> u_ex (fwd + branch compare -> redirect) -> u_if
(NOP mux on redirect) -> u_hazard (load-use) -> u_id (flush_id into
ID/EX rs?_val). The single-cycle multiplier is NOT critical, so it
stays single-cycle. Projected fitness ~12.12 * 46.5/5.44 * (1 - <1%
divide stall cost) ~= 100 iter/s (8x); the delta below is the schema cap.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. New module rtl/divider.sv: a restoring radix-2 (1 quotient bit/cycle)
   sequential divider for DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU. On start it latches
   |a|, |b| (abs only for signed ops), the result signs and the op; it
   runs 32 iterations of a 33-bit subtract/compare into a shifting
   {rem, quo} register, then applies the sign fix-up. RV32M corner cases
   fall out of the unsigned algorithm (x/0 -> quo=all-ones, rem=|a|;
   INT_MIN/-1 -> 0x80000000 / 0) provided the quotient negation is
   suppressed when b==0 (DIV by 0 must be -1 regardless of sign).
   Interface: start, op, a, b -> busy, done, result. `done` stays high
   (result held) until the EX/MEM register actually accepts it
   (i.e. until !stall_ex_mem), so a coincident dmem stall cannot lose it.
   Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS the same FSM/handshake is used but it
   completes after 2 cycles and returns the ALTOPS formula
   ((a-b)^const per op, computed from the latched operands) so formal
   still exercises the stall path inside the depth-20 BMC / liveness.
2. alu.sv: delete the combinational `/` and `%` arms (DIV* ops return
   the divider result via ex_stage instead). Replace mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su
   with ONE 33x33 signed multiply: a_ext = {sa & a[31], a},
   b_ext = {sb & b[31], b} with sa = (MULH|MULHSU), sb = MULH; MUL takes
   p[31:0], MULH/MULHSU/MULHU take p[63:32]. Keep the ALTOPS arms for the
   MUL ops unchanged.
3. ex_stage.sv: instantiate divider; is_div = valid && alu_op in
   {DIV,DIVU,REM,REMU}. start = is_div && !busy && !done. Output
   `ex_busy = is_div && !done` to the hazard unit. When ex_busy, the
   EX/MEM register captures a bubble (valid=0, ctrl.reg_write=0,
   mem_read/mem_write=0) instead of the div; when done (and not
   dmem-stalled) it captures the divider result as alu_result. Also
   export the post-forward rs1/rs2 so id_stage can refresh ID/EX
   operands while the div is held (see 4) — this keeps forwarding and
   RVFI rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata correct after the producers drain out of
   EX/MEM and MEM/WB during the ~33-cycle hold.
4. id_stage.sv: new input `hold_ex` (= ex_busy). While held, ID/EX keeps
   all fields but overwrites rs1_val/rs2_val with the EX-stage
   post-forward rs1/rs2 each cycle (always the architecturally correct
   value at that moment), so when the div finally leaves EX its
   recorded operands are right even though forwarding sources have
   changed.
5. hazard_unit.sv: new input ex_busy. stall_if |= ex_busy;
   stall_id |= ex_busy; flush_id must not assert due to ex_busy (the
   div's own ID/EX entry must be held, not bubbled). The instruction in
   IF/ID stays (PC held), exactly like a load-use stall. stall_ex_mem is
   NOT asserted by ex_busy (older instructions keep draining).
   Redirect cannot coincide with a div in EX (div is not a branch).
6. core.sv: wire ex_busy and the refresh path; no port changes.
TIMING DISCIPLINE (the new critical path runs redirect -> IF ->
hazard -> flush_id -> ID/EX): ex_busy must be a SHALLOW signal. Derive
it only from registered state: a 1-bit `id_ex_is_div` flop computed in
ID from the decoder (alu_op in DIV..REMU) and captured into ID/EX,
ANDed with ~div_done (a divider flop). Do not derive it from the
forwarded operands, the ALU result or `redirect`. Keep the divider's
33-bit subtract fed only from its own internal registers (never from
the forwarding muxes except at the one-cycle operand latch), so the
divider itself adds only a flop->sub->flop path (~10 ns). The ID/EX
operand-refresh mux adds one 2:1 mux level at the ID/EX rs?_val input
that sits on the current worst path's endpoint; implement it as part of
the existing enable/flush logic (select = registered-ish hold_ex) so it
does not lengthen the redirect->flush_id cone.
Expected: worst path drops from ~200 ns to ~27 ns (measured 46.5 MHz
with the divider stubbed out) with maybe a small loss for the
hold/refresh muxes. IPC
loss is ~33 cycles per executed divide, negligible in CoreMark's timed
region; the multiplier stays single-cycle so matrix kernels lose
nothing. LUT count should also drop substantially (four array
dividers + two redundant multipliers removed).

title: Multi-cycle M-extension unit: iterative divider + registered DSP multiplier off the EX critical path
motivation:
The baseline's worst path is 199.8 ns / 150 logic levels
(mem_wb.rd -> forward_unit -> ex operand mux -> alu -> BSRAM dmem
address). The depth comes from the single-cycle EX ALU, which holds
up to four 32-bit combinational array dividers (signed/unsigned
`/` and `%`) plus three 64-bit multipliers. They set Fmax at 5.44 MHz
and take most of the 12.3k LUT4s.
CoreMark's timed loop almost never divides, and MUL appears mainly in
core_matrix. So nearly every cycle pays the clock-period cost of a
circuit that is almost never used. No earlier experiment has touched
this; the log contains only the baseline.
With the divider and multiplier gone from EX, the longest remaining
path should be the ordinary 5-stage one:
  fwd compare -> 3:1 operand mux -> 32-bit carry-chain add/compare
  -> BSRAM address, or the branch redirect -> PC -> imem path.
That is about 15-25 levels, so Fmax should be roughly 7-10x higher.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move all eight RV32M operations out of the combinational ALU into a new
clocked unit, rtl/muldiv.sv. The unit is started from EX and stalls
the front of the pipeline with a busy/done handshake.

muldiv.sv (clock, reset, start, op[4:0], a, b, accept ->
           done, result[31:0], a_q, b_q):
  - IDLE: when `start` fires (an M-op is valid in EX and the unit is
    idle), latch op, a and b. These are the post-forward rs1/rs2
    values. Latch the raw values only; do abs/negate in the next cycle
    so the fwd-mux -> operand-register path stays short.
  - MUL / MULH / MULHU / MULHSU: stage 1 registers the 33-bit
    sign/zero-extended operands, chosen by op. Stage 2 registers the
    signed 33x33 product, which Gowin maps to DSP MULT36X36 with
    input/output registers. The result mux (lo or hi 32 bits) feeds
    `result`. Latency is 2-3 cycles. If the timing report shows the
    DSP path as critical, add one more register stage.
  - DIV / DIVU / REM / REMU: radix-2 restoring divider on
    magnitudes. It uses a 33-bit subtract and a 64-bit
    {remainder,quotient} shift register, one bit per cycle for 32
    cycles, followed by one sign-fixup cycle. The quotient is negated
    when the operand signs differ; the remainder takes the dividend's
    sign.
    Special cases:
      - divisor == 0: force quotient = 0xFFFFFFFF with no sign
        fixup. The remainder = dividend, which the algorithm already
        produces.
      - INT_MIN / -1 needs no special case: the magnitudes give
        q = 0x80000000 and r = 0, which is RV32M-correct.
  - DONE: hold `result` until `accept` (EX/MEM advancing, i.e. no
    dmem_stall), then return to IDLE. This guarantees that the same
    instruction cannot re-fire.
  - `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS: every M-op completes after 1 cycle
    with the ALTOPS formula computed from the latched operands. The
    formulas are the same ones alu.sv uses today, e.g.
    MUL = (a+b)^32'h5876063e. This still exercises the
    busy/stall/accept handshake under formal. It also keeps the insn,
    liveness and cover checks satisfiable within the depth-20 BMC; a
    33-cycle divider would not retire within that window.

Pipeline integration (in-order, one M-op in flight):
  - Decoder: new ctrl bit `is_muldiv`, set in the funct7 = 0000001
    OP arm. EX uses md_op = in.valid && in.ctrl.is_muldiv.
  - md_stall = md_op && !md_done. hazard_unit gets md_stall and does
    the following while it is high:
      - stall_if = 1 (PC holds)
      - stall_id = 1 and flush_id = 0 (ID/EX holds the M-op)
      - EX/MEM captures a bubble: valid = 0, reg_write = 0,
        mem_read/mem_write = 0. This lets the older instructions in
        MEM/WB drain and retire.
    dmem_stall keeps precedence: EX/MEM holds, and the unit keeps
    computing or stays in DONE.
  - When done: EX/MEM captures md result as alu_result. It MUST also
    take rs1_val/rs2_val from muldiv's latched a_q/b_q, not from the
    live forward mux. The forwarding producers may have drained into
    the regfile during the stall, which leaves ID/EX.rs?_val stale;
    riscv-formal `reg` and cosim would catch the wrong rs?_rdata. In
    the same cycle stall_id drops, so the next instruction enters EX
    the following cycle.
  - alu.sv: delete the `*`, `/` and `%` operators and both the real
    and ALTOPS M-ext arms. Add an input `md_result` and route it out
    of the existing op case mux for ALU_MUL..ALU_REMU. That reuses
    the existing result mux instead of adding a LUT level after the
    adder.
  - Neither redirect nor load-use can kill an M-op in EX. Redirect
    comes only from EX, and load-use looks only at LOADs in ID/EX, so
    the unit needs no abort path.

Expected results:
  - LUT4: about 12.3k -> 3-4k. The iterative divider costs ~150-250
    LUT plus about 100 FFs.
  - Fmax: 5.44 MHz -> at least 35 MHz, likely 40-60 MHz. The critical
    path becomes the forward -> adder -> BSRAM address path or the
    branch redirect path.
  - CPI cost: +2 cycles per MUL and about +34 per DIV. CoreMark -O3
    has few MULs per iteration (matrix kernel) and almost no divides
    in the timed region, so iter/cycle should fall by less than 3%.
Net fitness: roughly 12 -> 80-120 iter/s. The schema's +50% cap
understates this.

title: IF-stage BTB + bimodal counters + 4-entry RAS: zero-penalty correctly-predicted taken control flow
motivation:
Every taken branch, JAL and JALR costs 2 bubbles today: the redirect is only
resolved in EX and IF/ID are flushed (flush_if/flush_id on `redirect`), while
the fetch path itself is a plain "pc+4 unless EX redirects" (if_stage.sv).
In RV32IM -O3 CoreMark roughly 12-15% of dynamic instructions are taken
control transfers (list-walk loops in core_list_find/reverse, the
matrix inner loops, the crcu8 bit loop, core_state_transition's switch,
and many calls/returns into crcu8/crcu16/cmp_idx/cmp_complex). At ~1.55
CPI that is ~15-18% of all cycles spent in taken-branch bubbles.
The critical path (199.8 ns, fwd -> EX -> combinational divider -> EX/MEM)
is nowhere near fetch, so a fetch-side predictor is IPC gain at
essentially zero Fmax cost: its longest new paths (PC reg -> LUT-RAM read
-> tag compare -> next-PC mux, and the EX-side mispredict compare) are
on the order of 10-20 ns.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a branch predictor that is looked up in the same cycle the PC is
presented to imem, so a correctly predicted taken transfer has zero
penalty; EX verifies every prediction and only redirects on a mispredict.

1. New module rtl/branch_predictor.sv:
   - 64-entry direct-mapped BTB, index = pc[7:2], tag = pc[13:8] (6 bits).
     Entry payload (~29 bits): tag, target[19:2] (18 bits — all code lives in
     [0,0x100000); the predicted target is rebuilt as {12'b0,t,2'b00} and EX
     compares the FULL 32-bit target, so out-of-range targets merely
     mispredict), 2-bit saturating counter, kind {BRANCH, JAL, RET, JALR},
     is_call (rd==x1/x5).
     Payload array is `logic [28:0] mem [0:63]` with synchronous write and
     ASYNCHRONOUS read and no reset so Gowin infers distributed LUT-RAM
     (cheap); a separate 64-bit valid vector in flops is cleared on reset.
   - Prediction (combinational from the PC register):
     hit = valid[idx] && tag match; pred_taken = hit && (kind!=BRANCH || ctr[1]);
     pred_target = (kind==RET && ras_count!=0) ? ras_top : btb_target.
   - 4-entry return-address stack (circular, overwrite oldest on overflow).
     Push pc+4 when a hit entry has is_call; pop when kind==RET. RAS ops are
     gated on the fetch actually advancing: imem_ready && !stall_if &&
     !mispredict. No repair on mispredict — RAS corruption only costs
     performance, never correctness, because EX verifies the target.
   - Update port driven from EX (one write per cycle): on a valid,
     non-misaligned-fault branch/JAL/JALR in EX, gated by !stall_ex_mem.
     Taken transfers allocate/overwrite the entry (ctr = 2'b10 on allocate,
     saturating increment if the fetch-time lookup hit); not-taken branches
     only decrement the counter if the fetch-time lookup hit (never allocate).
     The fetch-time hit bit and counter are carried down the pipeline, so no
     second read port is needed.
2. if_stage.sv: next_pc = mispredict ? correct_pc
                        : pred_taken ? pred_target : pc + 4.

title: Shorten both 26.8ns EX cones: dedicated AGU, multiply-last ALU mux, redirect out of IF/load-use, narrow flush
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (hyp-001, 46.4 MHz, data path
21.5 ns after the 5.3 ns clock insertion) shows TWO tied critical cones, both
starting at the register-file BSRAM (cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s, tC2Q 2.26 ns):

Path 1 (26.836 ns) -> dmem BSRAM read address (ADB). The bench wrapper reads
dmem combinationally, so Gowin absorbs the EX/MEM alu_result flop into the
BSRAM address register and the address pins see the whole EX cone:
  RF -> id bypass LUT -> forward mux (3 LUTs: rs1_31_s10/s8/s7) -> alu_a mux
  -> mul_a sign LUT -> 33x33 DSP (1.1 ns net + 3.76 ns) -> 7-LUT result chain
  (n697_s12..s0 = ALU op case mux + is_jump/is_div mux) -> dmem_addr LUT ->
  BSRAM ADB[9].
A load/store only needs rs1+imm, yet its address waits on the multiplier.
Even with the address fixed, the same DSP -> 7-LUT chain ends at the EX/MEM
alu_result flops, only ~1.3 ns shorter.

Path 5 (26.816 ns, 52 cells) -> ID/EX rs1_val D input:
  RF -> bypass -> alu_b/rs2 forward LUTs -> 32-bit branch compare carry chain
  -> branch_taken/redirect (n929) -> u_if NOP mux on instr (n330, fanout 103)
  -> IF/ID rs2 field -> hazard load-use compare carry chain -> stall/flush
  logic -> ID/EX D mux (fanout 33) -> flop.
This is the same path that capped hyp-002 at 45.5 MHz after its MUL change,
which is why fixing only one cone gives nothing: both have to go.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Four cycle-neutral micro-optimizations that cut both cones (CPI and CoreMark
cycle count are unchanged; only Fmax moves):

1) Dedicated AGU. In EX add agu_addr = rs1 (post-forward) + in.imm with its
   own adder (no alu_src mux, no ALU result mux, no jump/div mux). Register it
   into a new EX/MEM field mem_addr. mem_stage uses in.mem_addr instead of
   in.alu_result for dmem_addr, byte_mask, misalignment, the load-extract
   shift and the RVFI aligned address. dmem address cone becomes
   RF -> bypass -> fwd mux -> 32-bit carry chain -> BSRAM (~9-10 ns data).

2) Multiply-last ALU result mux. Decode in ID (like is_div today) and register
   in ID/EX ctrl: is_mul, mul_hi (MULH/MULHSU/MULHU), mul_sa (MULH|MULHSU),
   mul_sb (MULH). Feed the multiplier from the post-forward rs1/rs2 (new alu
   ports ma/mb) rather than alu_a/alu_b, which removes the auipc/alu_src mux
   LUT from the DSP input. Build the result as
     early = link ? pc+4 : is_div ? div_result : base_alu_result
     out   = is_mul ? (mul_hi ? p[63:32] : p[31:0]) : early
   so the DSP output sees exactly one LUT(+MUX2_LUT5) before the EX/MEM flop,
   where it used to see 7. pc+4 (JAL/JALR link) and div_result come from
   flops and merge off the critical path. base_alu_result is the existing
   ADD/SUB/logic/SLT/shift/LUI case mux, no longer carrying the MUL arms.

3) Take `redirect` out of the IF -> decode -> load-use cone. if_stage emits
   NOP/valid=0 only on `flush` (= imem stall); flush_if = imem_stall. Safe
   because on every redirect cycle ID/EX is either bubbled (flush_id) or held
   (dmem_stall), so the IF payload is never captured. load_use needs
   id_ex.mem_read=1 while redirect needs id_ex branch/jump, and the decoder
   never sets both, so load_use is unaffected. The redirect then only
   drives the PC mux and flush_id.

4) Narrow flush. A redirect/load-use bubble in ID/EX clears only valid and
   the side-effect ctrl bits (reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch,
   is_jump, is_div, is_mul). Data fields (pc, rs1_val, rs2_val, imm, rd,
   rs*_addr, instr, other ctrl) just follow the stall enable. The flush net
   drops from ~150 flop D-muxes to ~8, and rs1_val/rs2_val lose their
   reset-mux LUT (path 5's endpoint). reset still clears everything. An
   invalid bubble with stale data is harmless: nothing downstream acts on
   it (no reg_write -> no forwarding, no mem op, no redirect, no div
   request, valid=0 -> no RVFI retirement).

Estimated new data path: about 14-15 ns for the ALU/MUL -> EX/MEM,
branch -> PC/flush and AGU -> BSRAM paths, versus 21.5 ns now. Allowing for
P&R noise that is 58-65 MHz, i.e. +25-40% fitness at identical IPC.

title: Lane-split EX: dedicated AGU for dmem address, late-select single-cycle MUL, ID-precomputed forward selects/results, redirect off the fetch->hazard path
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (46.4 MHz) shows two paths tied
at 26.8 ns, so fixing either one alone gains nothing. This is why hyp-002,
which only multi-cycled MUL, reached 45.5 MHz and lost IPC.
  Path 1 (MUL -> dmem address, 16 cells): regfile BSRAM DO (C2Q 2.26 ns)
    -> write-first bypass (1 LUT) -> forward mux (3 LUTs: s10/s8/s7,
    selects come from the forward_unit rd compares) -> alu_a AUIPC mux
    (1 LUT, fanout 30) -> mul_a sign-extend (fanout 72) -> DSP (3.76 ns)
    -> 7-LUT ALU case result mux (n697_s12..s0) -> jump/div mux -> BSRAM
    address register of dmem (dmem absorbs EX/MEM.alu_result).
  Path 5 (redirect, 26.8 ns): regfile -> bypass -> alu_b/rs2 forward
    -> 32-bit branch compare carry chain -> redirect -> if_stage NOP mux
    (fanout 103) -> hazard load-use rd compare (carry chain) -> ID/EX
    enable/flush -> ID/EX rs1_val (fanout 33).
About 60% of each path is control or muxing that is not needed on it. The
forward selects, AUIPC/LUI/link values and the result-class decode depend
only on flops of the previous stage. The multiplier product goes through
the entire ALU op mux and then drives the dmem address, even though a load
or store address is only rs1+imm. The redirect only needs to kill the
wrong-path slot, which flush_id already does, but it also goes through the
IF instruction mux and the load-use comparator.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure EX into parallel lanes whose results merge at one late,
flop-selected mux. Precompute everything operand-independent in ID. Keep
MUL single-cycle, so cycle count stays unchanged (lesson from hyp-002).

1. AGU lane. EX gets a dedicated adder mem_addr = rs1_fwd + imm. It is
   registered in a new EX/MEM.mem_addr field that alone drives
   io_dmemAddr, the byte mask, the misalign check and the RVFI aligned
   address in mem_stage. The dmem BSRAM address then sees
   fwd -> 32-bit add -> register, about 9 ns. EX/MEM.alu_result for
   loads and stores becomes don't-care: loads never forward from EX/MEM
   because of the load-use interlock.
2. Late-select MUL. alu.sv exports mul_out (hi/lo already selected, real
   and ALTOPS arms unchanged) and base_out (non-M ops) as separate ports.
   The existing `out` port stays for test_alu.py. mul_sa/mul_sb/mul_hi
   come from ID/EX flops. EX/MEM.alu_result becomes a one-hot AND-OR over
   {base_out, mul_out, div_result, pre_result}, with the one-hot selects
   registered in ID/EX. The DSP output then passes 1-2 LUTs, not 8, and
   ends at a FF instead of the dmem BSRAM.
3. ID-precomputed results. ID computes pre_result = LUI ? imm :
   AUIPC ? pc+imm : pc+4 (for JAL/JALR links) and branch_target = pc+imm.
   alu_a is then rs1_fwd with no AUIPC mux.
4. Registered forwarding selects. In ID, compare the decoding
   instruction's rs1/rs2 with ID/EX.rd (rd!=0, ctrl.reg_write) to get
   fwd_ex_q, and with EX/MEM.rd to get fwd_wb_q, then register the flags
   in ID/EX. In EX: sel_ex = fwd_ex_q & EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write, and
   sel_wb = fwd_wb_q & MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write & ~sel_ex. Gating on the
   producer's registered reg_write preserves the trap-cleared reg_write of
   misaligned JAL/JALR and misaligned loads.
   This is exact because ID/EX only captures when !dmem_stall && !ex_busy
   && !load_use. On exactly those cycles EX/MEM captures ID/EX and
   MEM/WB captures EX/MEM, so the producers the flags name are the ones
   that will be there. On every hold, those producers are frozen too.
5. Redirect off the fetch/hazard path. if_stage stops forcing the IF
   instruction to NOP on redirect; only imem_stall still does. flush_if
   drops `redirect`. load-use therefore compares raw instruction bits.
   Behaviour does not change: on redirect, PC takes redirect_target over
   stall, and flush_id (not held by dmem_stall) wins over stall_id in the
   ID/EX reset||flush priority. On flush, clear only ID/EX valid, ctrl,
   fwd flags and result-select flags (not the 32-bit data fields) to cut
   the flush_id fanout from ~200 FFs to ~30.

Estimated new worst paths: MUL about 13-14 ns (2.26 C2Q + bypass +
1-2 LUT forward + sign-extend + 3.76 DSP + 2 LUT), redirect about 12 ns,
shifter/add -> alu_result about 12 ns. That gives Fmax of about 60+ MHz,
+25-35%, at the same CoreMark cycle count.

title: Fetch BTB+bimodal with 1-cycle mispredict and registered wrong-path squash (no IF-NOP/hazard tail on redirect)
motivation:
Champion hyp-001 runs at 46.36 MHz and takes 4,491,817 cycles for 10 iterations.
Two paths are close to critical, both about 27 ns:
  (a) regfile/ID-EX -> fwd mux -> ALU adder -> dmem address   (26.8 ns, champion CP)
  (b) ID/EX -> fwd -> branch compare -> redirect -> if_stage NOP mux on
      out.instr -> hazard load-use compare -> stall_if/flush_id -> ID/EX and PC
      (26.8 ns in the hyp-001 probe; 27.9 ns CP in hyp-002)
Every taken branch, JAL and JALR costs one bubble. IF and ID are merged
(there is no IF/ID flop), so the only thing lost is the pc+4 instruction
that is being decoded while EX resolves.
Measured data: hyp-003-r1s2 added a 64-entry BTB, bimodal counters and a
4-entry RAS to the old core. That design keeps the 1-cycle mispredict
penalty, and cycles dropped from 4,491,485 to 4,186,137 (-6.8%, +7.3% IPC).
It did not win only because Fmax was still limited by the ~200 ns
combinational divider. Nobody has ported it to the divider-fixed core yet.
LESSONS.md warns that a port only pays off if no new path goes above
~27 ns. This hypothesis is built around that constraint: it adds the IPC
gain and also shortens path (b) instead of lengthening it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Port the fetch-stage predictor to the champion. Restructure the
redirect so the mispredict signal drives only the PC-register mux. The
wrong-path instruction is killed one cycle later by a FLOP (squash_q),
not by the combinational IF NOP mux, hazard unit and flush_id chain.

1. rtl/branch_predictor.sv (new). 64-entry direct-mapped BTB, index pc[7:2]
   and a partial tag pc[13:8]. The payload is target[19:2] (code is below
   1 MiB), a 2-bit bimodal counter, kind {BR, JAL, JALR} and is_call.
   Store the payload in LUT-RAM: async read, sync write, no reset. Keep a
   64-bit valid vector in flops that is cleared on reset. The lookup is
   combinational from the PC register:
     hit = valid & tag match
     pred_taken = hit & (kind != BR | ctr[1])
     pred_target = (kind==JALR & is_ret & ras_nonempty) ? ras_top : btb_target
   A 4-entry circular RAS pushes pc+4 on a predicted-taken is_call entry and
   pops on a predicted-taken return entry (JALR rs1=x1/x5, rd=x0). Gate both
   on the fetch actually advancing (!stall_if & imem_ready & !mispredict).
   RAS corruption only costs cycles because EX verifies every target.
   There is one update port, written from EX when the control instruction
   leaves EX (valid & !squash_q & !stall_ex_mem & !misalign_fault):
     - taken: allocate or overwrite the entry (ctr = 2'b10 on allocate,
       saturating increment on hit).
     - not-taken: decrement the counter, but only if the fetch-time lookup
       hit. The fetch-time hit and ctr ride down the pipe, so no second
       read port is needed.
2. rtl/if_stage.sv. The next-PC priority is:
     reset > mispredict (overrides every stall, as redirect does today)
     > stall_if (hold) > pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4
   REMOVE the `(flush || redirect)` NOP substitution on the redirect term.
   out.instr/valid is NOP-muxed only for imem_stall. The wrong-path
   instruction enters ID/EX normally and is squashed in EX. This cuts the
   redirect -> instr mux -> load-use -> flush_id/stall_if tail off path (b).
   IF/ID carries pred_taken, pred_target[31:2], pred_hit and pred_ctr.
3. rtl/id_stage.sv. Precompute in ID so EX needs no new adders on its
   critical cone:
     br_tgt   = pc + imm                        (B/JAL target; register it)
     pc4      = pc + 4                          (register it)
     tgt_ok   = (pc + imm == pred_target)       (B/JAL predicted-target check)
     jalr_exp = pred_target - imm               (JALR check: rs1 == jalr_exp
                                                 implies rs1+imm == pred_target)
   Latch these into ID/EX together with the prediction bits. Flush and
   reset clear them. Stall holds them.
4. rtl/ex_stage.sv. The mispredict term needs no 32-bit add before it:
     act_taken = misalign_fault ? 0 : (is_jump | branch_taken)
     mispredict_raw = valid & !squash_q & (
         is_branch ? (act_taken != pred_taken) | (act_taken & !tgt_ok)
       : is_jal    ? !act_taken | !pred_taken | !tgt_ok
       : is_jalr   ? act_taken != pred_taken | (act_taken & rs1_fwd != jalr_exp)
       :             pred_taken )                   // aliasing non-CTI
     correct_pc = !act_taken ? pc4_q : is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : br_tgt_q
   Assert the mispredict only when EX/MEM actually accepts the instruction
   (mispredict = mispredict_raw & !stall_ex_mem). During a dmem stall the
   branch just waits, which keeps the "one squash per mispredict" rule
   exact. Register squash_q <= mispredict. When squash_q=1, the instruction
   in ID/EX is the single wrong-path fetch:
     - clear its valid, reg_write, mem_read and mem_write into EX/MEM
     - suppress its own mispredict and its BTB update
     - gate ex_busy (a squashed DIV must not hold the pipe)
   squash_q and ex_busy stay flop-derived. RVFI pc_next/rd/trap fields
   still come from the resolved outcome, so the RVFI contract does not
   change.
5. rtl/hazard_unit.sv and rtl/core.sv. Replace `redirect` by `mispredict`
   for the PC only. Drop the redirect terms from flush_if/flush_id: the
   squash in EX does the kill. Load-use may insert one harmless extra
   bubble behind a squashed load; you may gate it with !squash_q. Wire
   the predictor, the update bundle and squash_q.

Why it helps:
- IPC: hyp-003 measured -6.8% cycles with the same 1-cycle mispredict
  penalty kept here.
- Fmax: path (b) loses its IF-NOP/hazard/ID-EX tail and ends at the PC
  flop. The JALR and target checks are equality compares against
  ID-precomputed values, not adders. New fetch loop:
    PC flop -> LUT-RAM read -> 6-bit tag compare -> 32-bit next-PC mux -> PC
  That is about 8-10 levels.
Fmax is expected to stay about 46 MHz (still bounded by path (a)), with a
small upside from path (b) no longer competing for placement.
Estimate: 4.49M -> about 4.19M cycles, fitness about 103 -> 109-111.

title: Move the regfile out of BSRAM so EX starts from fabric flops, and trim the tails of the MUL and branch->PC paths
motivation:
Gowin timing of the champion (r2s1, placement 0: 63.8 MHz, data path
15.64 ns) shows that all 25 worst setup paths start at
cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s[0]/DO. Gowin maps the 32x32 regfile onto two
BSRAMs (one per read port) and absorbs the ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val
registers into the BSRAM read register. The write-first bypass then
becomes a LUT after the RAM (u_id/id_ex_w.rs?_val_*_s109). Every EX cone
therefore starts with:
  BSRAM tC2Q 2.260 ns + route 0.76-0.93 + bypass LUT 0.37-0.56 +
  route 0.69-0.96  = ~4.3 ns before the forward mux,
where a fabric DFF would reach the forward mux in ~1.1 ns. Three cones
are tied at ~15.6 ns and all share this start:
  (1) fwd mux (2 LUT) -> alu_b imm mux -> 33x33 DSP (3.78 ns) ->
      3-LUT one-hot result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result
  (2) fwd mux -> 32-bit carry-chain compare (1.64 ns) -> 4 LUTs of
      redirect/enable logic (u_if/n69_*) -> PC CE (fanout 30)
  (3) the same compare -> redirect -> flush_id -> ID/EX sync reset.
LESSONS: tied cones must be fixed in the same iteration, and the r2s1
lesson says the next step must shorten branch-resolve -> PC itself.

Everything below is cycle-neutral (CoreMark cycle count unchanged at
4,491,817). Only Fmax changes.

1. Distributed regfile (main cut). Force regs[] out of BSRAM with
   (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) (fall back to "registers" if
   Gowin still infers BSRAM). Keep the combinational read and the
   write-first bypass, but resolve both in ID *before* the ID/EX
   rs1_val/rs2_val flops, so these become plain fabric DFFs. Remove the
   per-entry reset loop, which blocks any RAM mapping. Keep read-as-zero
   for never-written registers with a 32-bit written-valid flop vector
   that resets to 0 and is set on write. Architectural behaviour after
   reset stays exactly as today for formal and cosim. The new ID-side
   path is imem_data -> LUT-RAM read (~2 ns) -> bypass/valid -> ID/EX,
   which is far from critical. Expected saving is ~3 ns on all three
   tied cones.
2. MUL tail. Feed the multiplier's b operand from post-forward rs2
   instead of alu_b (M ops never use the immediate), which removes one
   LUT plus a route (~1.3 ns) before the DSP. Register sel_mul_lo and
   sel_mul_hi in ID and build EX/MEM.alu_result as a single final 5-input
   select: {sel_mul_hi, sel_mul_lo, p[63:32][i], p[31:0][i], early[i]},
   where early = base|div|pre OR-merge is computed in parallel. This
   leaves the DSP output one LUT5 away from the flop instead of 3 LUTs.
3. Branch -> PC tail. Precompute in ID and register into ID/EX:
   one-hot branch selects (beq/bne/blt/bge/bltu/bgeu, already ANDed with
   is_branch and with !branch_target[1]), jal_ok (JAL with an aligned
   target), and the non-redirect PC enable terms that are independent
   of EX operands. In EX, redirect becomes an AND-OR of the one-hots
   with {eq, !eq, lt, !lt, ltu, !ltu} plus jal_ok, plus the JALR term
   (is_jalr & !agu_sum[1]). That is at most 2 LUTs after the compare
   outputs into the PC enable and flush_id. Misalign trap semantics and
   pc_next are unchanged. The trap flag can be computed off the
   redirect path.

Estimated result: the tied cones fall from ~15.6 ns to ~12-12.5 ns
(item 1), and items 2 and 3 keep MUL and branch from becoming the new
single limiter. Expected median Fmax ~76-80 MHz vs 68.0, which is
+12-17% fitness at unchanged cycles. Cost is ~32 RAM16SDP4 LUT-RAMs plus
32 valid flops. The 2 BSRAMs are freed. Area is well inside 10k LUT4.

title: Bypass network moved to the ID->EX boundary: EX operands come from plain flops (async LUT-RAM regfile read + 4-source forward mux into ID/EX)
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (hyp-20260929-002-r2s1)
with place option 0: 63.8 MHz, 15.64 ns data delay. All 25 listed
setup paths start at the register-file BSRAM (cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s
/ _s0 DO[*]) and end within 0.25 ns of each other. They split into
three cones:
  - path 1/5: regfile -> MUL/ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result
  - paths 2, 6-8, 13, 16-20: regfile -> branch compare -> redirect ->
    u_if/pc CE/D
  - paths 3-4, 9-12, 14: regfile -> redirect -> flush_id -> ID/EX
    ctrl/fwd RESET
Synthesis made ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val into the BSRAM output register.
So every EX cone pays the same prefix before any real work. Measured on
path 2:
  - BSRAM tC2Q: 2.260 ns
  - u_id id_ex_w.rs1_val_0_s109 hold/bypass LUT: 0.761 + 0.555 ns
  - u_ex rs1_0_s1 / rs1_0_s0 forward mux: 0.688 + 0.371 + 1.230
    + 0.555 ns
That totals 6.42 ns of 15.64 (41%) before the branch comparator's
first carry cell (n694_s1). A plain flop would be about 0.4 ns C2Q
plus about 0.7 ns route.
Because the three cones are tied, cutting one of them (multi-cycling
MUL, or registering the redirect) only exposes the next one and costs
cycles; see the r1s1 and r2s0 lessons. Removing the shared prefix
shortens all of them at once at zero cycle cost.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the bypass network in the VexRiscv style. The forward
muxes move from the start of EX to the end of ID, so the ID/EX
rs1_val/rs2_val flops hold operands that are already fully
forwarded. Every EX lane then starts from a plain FF.

1. Register file (rtl/reg_file.sv): keep the combinational read
   addressed by the IF instruction's rs1/rs2 fields. Drop the
   write-first bypass from the file itself (the WB forward source
   below covers it). The read now feeds a mux, not a flop, so
   synthesis must implement it as async LUT-RAM (or FFs). It cannot
   be absorbed into ID/EX as a registered-read RAM. The reset loop
   can go: x0 is forced to 0 on read, and there is no reset
   requirement on x1..x31 (cosim/formal start from reset, and the
   programs initialize registers before use). If removing it breaks
   anything, keep it.
2. ID forward mux (rtl/forward_unit.sv + rtl/id_stage.sv). For each
   of rs1/rs2 of the decoding instruction, compare with rd != 0 in
   this priority order:
     a. ID/EX.rd && ID/EX.ctrl.reg_write && ID/EX.valid: take the EX
        result. This is the same one-hot AND-OR value that EX writes
        into EX/MEM.alu_result (base_out | mul_out | div_result |
        pre_result), exported from ex_stage as `ex_result`. A LOAD
        in EX never reaches here because the load-use interlock
        bubbles.
     b. EX/MEM.rd && reg_write (trap-cleared): take the MEM result,
        mem_to_reg ? load_data (from mem_stage, the aligned and
        sign/zero-extended dmem word) : EX/MEM.alu_result.
     c. MEM/WB: take wb_w_data when wb_w_en (this replaces the
        regfile write-first bypass).
     d. Otherwise take the regfile read.
   The compares depend only on IF-instr bits and stage rd/ctrl flops,
   so the selects settle early. The late-arriving ex_result must sit
   at the LAST mux level (operand = sel_ex ? ex_result : rest), one
   LUT before the ID/EX flop. mul_out and div_result stay one-hot
   lanes and are not re-muxed through the base ALU.
   ID/EX captures on the same !stall condition as today. ID/EX, EX/MEM
   and MEM/WB advance together, and every capture edge is a cycle on
   which the producer ahead has a final value:
     - A dmem stall holds all three registers.
     - ex_busy holds ID/EX until div_done. On the release edge
       ex_result = div_result.
     - Load-use bubbles for one cycle, so the next cycle the LOAD is
       in MEM and path b supplies load_data.
   So the captured operand is architecturally exact, and it stays
   valid for however long the instruction then sits in EX.
3. EX (rtl/ex_stage.sv). Delete the forward mux and the
   fwd_ex_mem/fwd_mem_wb inputs. rs1 = in.rs1_val and
   rs2 = in.rs2_val go straight into the ALU, the DSP, the AGU
   adder, the branch comparator and the divider. The div_rs1_q/
   div_rs2_q RVFI shadow flops can go, because ID/EX now holds the
   exact operands for the whole divide. Export ex_result. The
   one-hot selects, AGU lane, pre_result/branch_target precompute,
   misalign traps and redirect logic are unchanged.
4. The hazard unit, the pipeline depth, the branch penalty and the
   load-use penalty are all unchanged, so the cycle count should
   equal the champion's 4,491,817.

Expected timing effect. Every EX cone loses the measured 6.4 ns
prefix and gains back about 1.1 ns (FF C2Q plus route). The EX-result
-> ID/EX forward path also gains one LUT plus route, about 1.2 ns.
That brings the 15.6 ns cones to roughly 9.5-11 ns.
  - MUL becomes FF -> DSP -> AND-OR, which forks to the EX/MEM flop
    and to the last-level ID forward LUT -> ID/EX flop.
  - Branch becomes FF -> 32-bit compare -> redirect -> PC mux.
  - AGU becomes FF -> add -> dmem BSRAM address register.
The new ID-side paths are short:
  - IF instr -> LUT-RAM read (~2 ns) -> 2 mux LUTs -> FF.
  - IF instr -> rd compare -> select.
  - dmem BSRAM DO -> load align/extend (2-3 LUTs) -> 1 fwd LUT -> FF,
    about 8 ns.
None of them should exceed ~11 ns. Target: about 85-90 MHz at
unchanged cycles, i.e. +25-30%.
Implementation guard: the regfile must NOT be re-absorbed into a
registered-read BSRAM. Check the synthesis report (the BSRAM count
should drop by the regfile's blocks). Also check that the new
worst path no longer starts at cpu/u_rf/regs_regs*.

title: Zero-bubble fetch/decode predictor: JAL + BTFN-agree bimodal branches, pc+imm target, direction-only EX check
motivation:
Every taken branch and every JAL/JALR costs a 1-cycle bubble in the
champion (hyp-002-r2s1, 151.41 iter/s, 68.0 MHz, 4,491,817 cycles). The
redirect comes from EX, and flush_id kills the pc+4 slot fetched behind
the control instruction.
hyp-003-r1s2 and hyp-003-r2s2 measured this bubble. A 64-entry BTB with
bimodal counters and a 4-entry RAS cut cycles 4.49M -> 4.19M (-6.8%).
The IPC gain survived timing only when the redirect tail was cut with a
flop. r2s2 still lost because it was built on the slower hyp-001 base.
It also carried a lot of timing risk: a PC -> LUT-RAM -> tag compare ->
next-PC loop, target compares in EX, and a squash_q restructure.
This core has no IF/ID register: IF and ID are the same cycle. The
instruction word is therefore available (io_imemData, an LFSR flop in
the timed bench) in the same cycle as its PC. A decode-time predictor can
steer the next PC with ZERO bubble, the same as a BTB hit, for every
direct branch and JAL. It needs no target storage, has no cold misses
and no tag aliasing. Its target pc+imm is exact by construction, so EX
only has to check the DIRECTION, and that check is a flop-XOR on the
existing branch_cond. The EX -> PC redirect path gains no logic level.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict in the merged IF/ID cycle from the fetched instruction. Verify
the direction only in EX. Keep the champion's kill mechanism: redirect
plus flush_id kills exactly one slot.

1. Fetch/decode predictor (new rtl/fetch_pred.sv, instantiated in
   if_stage or core). Pre-decode the IF/ID instruction only when
   out.valid (imem delivered):
     is_jal = opcode 1101111
     is_br  = opcode 1100011 && funct3 not in {2,3}
     imm    = is_jal ? J-imm : B-imm      (narrow extract, no full imm_gen)
     tgt    = pc + imm                    (dedicated 32-bit adder)
     tgt_ok = (imm[1] == 0)               (never predict a misaligned target)
   Direction table: 128 x 2-bit "agree-with-BTFN" counters indexed by
   pc[8:2]. They are in flops reset to 2'b00 (strongly agree), or in
   LUT-RAM with zero init. The read is combinational from the PC flop,
   in parallel with pre-decode:
     dir_br    = instr[31] ^ ctr[1]    (cold state = backward-taken /
                                        forward-not-taken)
     pred_taken = tgt_ok && (is_jal || (is_br && dir_br))
   if_stage PC priority:
     reset > redirect (EX) > stall_if (hold) > pred_taken ? tgt : pc+4
   The late EX redirect stays on the LAST mux level. The pred_taken /
   tgt select sits behind it and starts from flops (the PC register and
   the imem data flop): about 10-12 ns, well under the 21 ns critical
   path. No RAS and no JALR prediction: CoreMark returns are about
   2k/iteration against about 30k taken branches/JALs. JALR keeps the
   champion's EX redirect unchanged.
2. id_stage. Latch pred_taken into ID/EX (new id_ex_t.pred_taken; flush
   and reset clear it). Also latch a registered br_tgt_misalign =
   pc_imm[1] for the branch misalign check. pre_result already equals
   pc+4 for branches (sel_pre=0 there), so it serves as the
   "predicted taken but not taken" fall-through target. No new 32-bit
   field is needed.
   Invariant: whenever ID/EX captures a valid instruction, the PC
   advanced with that same instruction's prediction in the same cycle.
   Both enables are !stall_id && !flush_id versus !stall_if. They differ
   only on imem stall, when the slot is an invalid NOP. So pred_taken in
   ID/EX exactly describes what fetch did.
3. ex_stage redirect. It is the same depth as today: the XOR with a flop
   folds into the LUT that already ANDs is_branch.
     br_redir  = is_branch & (pred_taken_q ? !branch_cond
                                           : branch_cond & !br_tgt_misalign_q)
     jal_redir = is_jump & !is_jalr & !pred_taken_q & !misalign_jump
                 (JAL is only unpredicted when its target is misaligned,
                  which traps; this is kept as a safety net)
     jalr_redir = is_jalr & !misalign_jump      (unchanged)
     redirect_target = is_jump ? jump_target
                     : pred_taken_q ? pre_result (pc+4) : branch_target
   The inner mux is selected by flops over flop data, so the agu_sum ->
   PC data path does not get deeper. EX/MEM.pc_next, the misalign trap
   rules and all RVFI fields stay as the RESOLVED outcome and are
   unchanged. flush_id = (load_use | redirect) & !dmem_stall is
   unchanged. A predicted-taken branch that falls through redirects to
   pc+4 and kills the target slot. A correctly predicted branch or JAL
   does not redirect, so the target instruction in IF/ID is kept.
4. Counter update, OFF the EX critical cone. It uses the registered
   EX/MEM fields: when EX/MEM.valid && ctrl.is_branch && !trap, write
   ctr[EX/MEM.pc[8:2]] = sat(ctr +/- 1) with the direction
   agree = (branch_taken == instr[31]). ctr is read from the table's
   second read port, or carried down from fetch. Re-writing the same
   value while EX/MEM is held by a dmem stall is idempotent, or gate the
   write with !stall_ex_mem.
MEASURED with the Python ISS on the -O3 2K CoreMark ELF (2.94M
instructions, 10 iterations): 295,904 taken branches, 236,442 not-taken
branches, 49,629 JALs and 13,794 JALRs (13,772 of them returns). Today
that is 359,327 bubbles. Pure BTFN plus JAL leaves 125,584 bubbles
(-233.7k). The 128-entry BTFN-agree bimodal table leaves 63,200 bubbles
(49,406 branch mispredicts plus the JALRs), -296.1k. That is -6.6% of
the 4,491,817 cycles, about the same as the r1s2 BTB (-305k).
Expected result: cycles fall about 6.6%. All JALs (calls, loop
back-edges, if/else joins) and most loop back-edges become zero-bubble;
the bimodal counters recover data-dependent forward branches. Loss
against the r1s2 BTB comes only from returns (JALR), about 0.5%. Fmax
stays flat: the champion's 20.97 ns regfile -> alu_result path and the
branch_cond -> redirect -> PC path get no added levels. The new
fetch-side paths start at flops and are about 10-12 ns. Area is about
+300-450 LUT4 and +130-260 FF.

changes.description:
New module. It pre-decodes JAL/BRANCH from the IF/ID instruction,
forms the J/B immediate and a dedicated pc+imm adder, and checks
target alignment (imm[1]==0). It holds the 128-entry 2-bit
agree-with-BTFN counter table indexed by pc[8:2]: flops with
synchronous reset to 2'b00, or zero-init LUT-RAM. Outputs are
pred_taken and pred_target. The update port is driven from
registered EX/MEM fields (pc[8:2], branch_taken, instr[31],
valid && is_branch && !trap).

(pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4). Redirect stays on the final mux
level. Only predict when the slot is valid (imem ready). Export
pred_taken in the IF/ID bundle.

                : pred_q ? pre_result : branch_target.

pred_taken/pred_target to if_stage, update port from the EX/MEM
register (pc, branch_taken, instr[31], valid, ctrl.is_branch,

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-003-r3s2 (regression, -7.07%): The zero-bubble decode-time JAL + BTFN-agree bimodal predictor delivered the cycle cut its ISS bubble count forecast (140.70 iter/s at 59.1 MHz implies ~4.20M cycles, -6.5% vs 4.49M), but Fmax fell from 68.0 to 59.1 MHz (-13%) even though the new worst path (regfile -> ALU -> alu_result, 22.3 ns vs the champion's 20.97 ns) contains no predictor logic, so the most likely cause is placement pressure from +385 LUT / +277 FF (a 256-flop counter table with a second read port for EX/MEM training, plus a dedicated pc+imm adder) on a ~2.4k-LUT core whose EX cones are tied; ISS bubble counts are therefore a trustworthy cycle forecast, but a ~6-7% IPC gain leaves almost no Fmax budget (it must lose less than ~2% to clear the 4.6% bar), so a retry should first cut the area (counters in LUT-RAM or carried down the pipe for a single read port, 64 entries) and be rebased onto the 80.6 MHz r3s1 champion.

title: Cut the three tied 11.7 ns cones: DSP product registered at the EX end (mul-use interlock), flat one-hot ALU lanes, flat pre-decoded load extract
motivation:
A fresh `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (hyp-002-r3s1,
179.43 iter/s; option-0 Fmax 84.7 MHz) shows three separate cones tied
within 0.1 ns of data delay. They fill the whole top 25; the arrival
times include 5.33 ns of clock insertion.
  A. MUL, 11.77 ns (paths 1-6, 8, 10+): rs2_val_31 -> alu_b mux LUT ->
     mul_b[32] sign LUT -> DSP (3.78 ns) -> 3 LUTs (hi/lo mux + one-hot
     AND-OR) -> EX/MEM.alu_result, or +1 forward LUT -> ID/EX rs?_val.
  B. LOAD, 11.71 ns (paths 7, 23): dmem BSRAM DO (tC2Q 2.26 ns) ->
     shifted (2 LUT) -> load_data sext/zext (3 LUT) -> mem_fwd mux +
     rs_early + ex-level forward (3 LUT) -> ID/EX rs1_val.
  C. BASE ALU, 11.68 ns (path 9): rs1_val_26 -> shifter (2 LUT) ->
     base_out case over the 5-bit op (3 LUT) -> one-hot AND-OR (2 LUT)
     -> forward LUT -> ID/EX rs2_val.
LESSONS r2s0 and r2s1 showed that tied cones must be cut in the same
iteration: cutting only one of them buys ~0 Fmax. hyp-002-r1s1
multi-cycled MUL when it was NOT critical and lost +188k cycles (2-3
stall cycles on every MUL, i.e. ~63-94k MULs). It is critical now,
and a pipelined MUL costs at most 1 cycle, only for a directly
dependent next instruction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three cycle-neutral or near-neutral cuts, one per cone. After them no
EX or MEM cone should exceed ~9-9.5 ns data delay.

A. MUL split across EX/MEM (treated like a load).
   - ID precomputes registered sign-extension bits
     mul_a_sx = (MULH|MULHSU) & rs1_fwd[31] and
     mul_b_sx = MULH & rs2_fwd[31]. Fold each into the last-level
     forward LUT, e.g. sa & (sel_ex ? ex_result[31] : early[31]) fits
     one LUT4. Also register one-hot sel_mul_lo (MUL) and sel_mul_hi
     (MULH*).
   - EX feeds the DSP {mul_a_sx, rs1_val} x {mul_b_sx, rs2_val}
     straight from the ID/EX flops, not through alu_b. The full 64-bit
     product goes into new EX/MEM.mul_p on the same !stall enable, so
     Gowin can pack it into the DSP output register with CE. Remove
     the mul lane from ex_result/alu_result entirely: sel_base,
     sel_div and sel_pre are 0 for MUL, so alu_result = 0.
   - MEM: alu_or_mul = alu_result | (sel_lo_q & p[31:0])
     | (sel_hi_q & p[63:32]). It feeds the non-load forward and
     MEM/WB.alu_result, so WB, the regfile and RVFI rd_wdata are
     unchanged.
   - hazard_unit: the load-use term uses a registered ID/EX bit
     late_result = mem_read | is_mul instead of mem_read. The
     compare depth is unchanged.
   - ALTOPS: the (a+b)^const or (a-b)^const stand-in is registered
     into mul_p[31:0] with sel_lo, so formal sees the same interlock
     and forwarding timing. The real and ALTOPS branches stay
     consistent.
C. Flat base-ALU lanes. Replace the base_out case mux and the separate
   4-lane AND-OR with one AND-OR whose one-hot selects are ID/EX flops
   decoded in ID:
     add/sub lane: one adder, b inverted by registered sub
     logic lane:   per-bit LUT4 {a,b,lop[1:0]}, lop = 00 zero / AND /
                   OR / XOR, so the lane is pre-gated with no extra AND
     shift lane:   SLL/SRL/SRA with registered dir/arith bits
     slt lane:     bit 0 only (SLT/SLTU)
     pre_result:   LUI, AUIPC, link, as today
     div lane:     as today
   LUI already rides pre_result. The ALU becomes lane -> 2-level
   AND-OR -> forward LUT: about 3 fewer LUT levels than the current
   case (3) + AND-OR (2).
B. Flat load extraction. EX decodes agu_sum[1:0] (the early carry
   bits) with mem_width/mem_sext into registered EX/MEM one-hot byte
   selects:
     b0_sel[3:0]: which rdata byte feeds result byte 0
     b1_sel:      rdata[15:8] / rdata[31:24] / fill
     hi_word:     result[31:16] = rdata[31:16]
     sgn_sel[1:0]: which of rdata[7]/[15]/[23]/[31] is the sign
     fill_s:      sign fill
   load_data is then a flat AND-OR of rdata lanes plus the fill.
   The sign is one mux4 level. About 3 LUT levels instead of 5.
   In ID, move the MEM-stage load value to the LAST forward level next
   to ex_result:
     rs_fwd = sel_ex ? ex_result
            : sel_ld ? load_data
            : early(EX/MEM alu_or_mul / MEM/WB / regfile)
   sel_ld = sel_mem & EX/MEM.mem_to_reg & !sel_ex is computed on the
   select side only (IF-instr bits and stage flops), so neither data
   input gets deeper.

Expected: the MUL cone becomes flop -> DSP -> OREG (~6 ns). The load
cone becomes 2.26 + ~3 extract LUTs + 1-2 forward LUTs (~8.5-9 ns).
The ALU cone becomes ~8.5-9 ns. The next limiter is likely the branch
compare -> redirect -> PC path or the AGU -> BSRAM address path, which
the report puts below the top 25 (>~11.4 ns data or less). Fmax gain
+15-22% (median ~93-98 MHz vs 80.6). Cycles rise ~1-1.5% (only a
MUL -> immediate-consumer pair pays one cycle; MUL, independent, use
forwards from EX/MEM). Area is roughly neutral: 64 product flops sit
in the DSP OREG, the case mux is removed, a few select flops are
added.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-001-r4s0 (improvement, +31.15%): Cutting all three tied ~11.7 ns cones in one change is the new champion at 235.32 vs 179.43, more than twice its +13% forecast. The three cuts were: registering the full 64-bit DSP product into EX/MEM.mul_p on the !stall enable, with MEM picking the half and a registered ID/EX late_result = mem_read | is_mul folding MUL into the load-use interlock; flat one-hot ALU lanes with ID-decoded selects in place of the case-over-op plus AND-OR; and one-hot load byte selects decoded in EX with the load value moved to the last forward level. If cycles rose only the designed ~1%, this implies about 106-107 MHz vs 80.6, which confirms r3s1's diagnosis that the single-cycle ALU/MUL -> ex_result -> forward -> ID/EX loop was the limiter, and it shows that a pipelined MUL behind a one-cycle mul-use interlock is cheap once the DSP is critical (unlike r1s1's 2-3-cycle multi-cycle MUL); the branch-compare -> PC and AGU -> BSRAM paths evidently sat well below the ~11.4 ns the forecast assumed, so the next step needs a fresh timing report to find the new limiter.

title: Late-result lanes: 2-stage MUL (EX->MEM, mul-use interlock), registered-select load extract, flattened one-hot EX result
motivation:
I re-ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (hyp-002-r3s1,
179.43 iter/s, median 80.6 MHz; place_option 0 gives 84.7 MHz, 11.77 ns
of data delay). All 25 worst setup endpoints fall into THREE cones, tied
within 0.1 ns. All three end at the ID/EX operand flops (through the ID
forward mux) or at EX/MEM.alu_result:
  1. MUL (11.77 ns): ID/EX.rs2_val[31] -> alu_b imm/rs2 mux -> mul_b[32]
     sign LUT -> DSP B[33]->DOUT (3.78 ns) -> hi/lo select -> one-hot
     result AND-OR (3 LUTs) -> EX/MEM.alu_result, and via ex_result ->
     the ID forward LUT -> ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val.
  2. LOAD (11.71 ns): dmem BSRAM DO (tC2Q 2.26 ns) -> shifted (2 LUTs)
     -> load_data width/sign (3 LUTs; the sign bit has fanout 18) ->
     fwd_data -> ID rs_fwd (3 LUTs: mem/wb/rf, then ex) -> ID/EX.
  3. ALU loop (11.68 ns): ID/EX.rs1_val[26] (fanout 18, 3.58 ns of
     routing) -> shifter (2 LUTs) -> base case mux + one-hot result
     (5 LUTs) -> ex_result -> ID rs_fwd -> ID/EX.
The r2s0 lesson says tied critical cones must be fixed in the same
iteration. A MUL-only fix would leave the core at about 11.7 ns (+0%).
The r3s1 lesson already predicted cone 1: with operands in plain flops,
the result lanes set the clock, so the lanes themselves must get
shorter. The r1s1 caution (don't multi-cycle MUL unless it is critical)
no longer applies, because the DSP is now on the worst path. CoreMark
runs only about 1-2k MULs per iteration against about 449k cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure where the late results are produced. Long-latency producers
(MUL, load) finish in MEM with every select precomputed and registered.
The single-cycle ALU loop keeps only flat, flop-selected lanes.

A. Two-stage MUL lane (the structural core).
   M1 (EX): the DSP reads the ID/EX operands, never the immediate (MUL
   has none, so the alu_b mux leaves this path):
     a = {mul_sa_q & rs1[31], rs1},  b = {mul_sb_q & rs2[31], rs2}
   mul_sa_q, mul_sb_q and mul_hi_q are new ID-decoded ID/EX flags. The
   raw 64-bit product goes straight into a new EX/MEM field mul_p
   (enable !stall, no logic in between, so Gowin can pack it into the
   DSP output register). EX's one-hot result drops the MUL lane, so the
   DSP is no longer in ex_result, EX/MEM.alu_result or the ID forward
   loop. Optional: give the DSP dedicated ID/EX operand copies (the
   rs_fwd value captured twice) so the ALU/AGU/branch operand flops lose
   fanout. This also targets cone 3's 3.58 ns fanout route.
   M2 (MEM): mul_res = mul_hi_q ? mul_p[63:32] : mul_p[31:0], then
   alu_or_mul = is_mul_q ? mul_res : alu_result. Both come from flops
   and run in parallel with the BSRAM read. MEM/WB.alu_result, fwd_data,
   wb_w_data and RVFI rd_wdata all see the product.
   Hazard: generalize load-use to late-result use with a registered
   ID/EX flag late_rd = mem_read | is_mul, which keeps the compare the
   same depth. A MUL whose rd is read by the very next instruction gets
   the same single bubble as a load. The EX forward select may still
   fire on the MUL, but flush_id kills that slot, the same argument the
   load path already uses.
B. Load extraction from registered byte-lane selects. In EX, compute
   one-hot per-lane controls from mem_width, mem_sext and agu_sum[1:0]
   (a 2-bit add of flops) and register them into EX/MEM:
     b0src[3:0]  (lane feeding result byte 0)
     b1src       (lane 1 for LH@0 / LW, lane 3 for LH@2)
     hi_word     (bytes 2-3 from lanes 2-3)
     sgn_lane[3:0] + sext (sign bit source), fill16 / fill8 (fill width)
   Then load_data is AND-OR of DO bytes (2 levels), and the fill is
   (OR of DO msb & sgn_lane) & sext (2 levels) merged in a 3rd level.
   That is 3 LUT levels, down from 5. In MEM, fwd_data =
   mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_or_mul keeps a single level. In ID,
   reorder the operand mux so load data enters at the LAST level with
   ex_result:
     rs_fwd = sel_ex ? ex_result : sel_ld ? load_data : early
   where early = sel_mem_alu ? mem alu_or_mul : sel_wb ? wb : rf
   is computed in parallel, and sel_ld = sel_mem & EX/MEM.mem_to_reg.
   This cuts the ID part of cone 2 from 3 levels to 1 (LUT5).
C. Flatten the EX one-hot result. ID decodes registered lane selects
   sel_add (ADD/SUB, with the sub bit registered), sel_logic (AND/OR/XOR,
   with a registered 2-bit sub-op), sel_shift (SLL/SRL/SRA, with
   registered dir/arith), sel_slt (SLT/SLTU, 1 bit into result[0]),
   sel_pre, sel_div. result = AND-OR of those lanes, with no 5-bit alu_op
   case in the loop: 2 levels after the slowest lane instead of the
   current 5. It remains ex_result, still at the last LUT of the ID
   forward mux.

Expected timing: cone 1 moves to about 7 ns (flop -> sign LUT -> DSP
-> flop), cone 2 to about 9.5 ns (tC2Q 2.26 + 3 extract + 1 forward),
and cone 3 to about 10 ns (-2 LUT levels). The unseen fourth cone
(branch compare -> redirect -> PC/flush, or LFSR instr -> decode ->
forward selects) was not in the top 25, so its data delay is under
about 11.5 ns, and its exact value is unknown. That points to about 10-10.5 ns, roughly 90-95 MHz on the
median placement against 80.6 today. Cycles grow by at most 0.5% (MUL
followed directly by a consumer), and loads are unchanged. Net fitness
is about +10-15%.

load_data and mem_alu_or_mul from mem_stage (in place of
mem_fwd_data), plus EX/MEM mem_to_reg for sel_ld.

Split sel*_mem into sel*_ld (EX/MEM mem_to_reg) and sel*_mem_alu,
both from rd compares and registered EX/MEM ctrl, so the depth is
unchanged.

DSP operands come from the ID/EX flops (or dedicated copies) plus
registered sign bits. Register the raw product into EX/MEM.mul_p
with nothing in between. result/ex_result = flat one-hot AND-OR of
add/logic/shift/slt/pre/div lanes (no mul). Compute and register the
load byte-lane selects from agu_sum[1:0], mem_width and mem_sext.
Branch, AGU, redirect, misalign, divider and EX/MEM capture
semantics are unchanged.

load_data = AND-OR of dmem_rdata bytes with the registered lane
selects, plus the sign/zero fill (3 LUT levels). mul_res and
alu_or_mul come from flops. Export load_data and alu_or_mul
separately for the ID mux, and keep fwd_w_en. MEM/WB.read_data and
MEM/WB.alu_result capture load_data and alu_or_mul. dmem ports,
misalign trap and RVFI fields are unchanged.

Rewire: id_ex_w.late_rd to hazard_unit; load_data and alu_or_mul
from u_mem to u_id; EX/MEM mem_to_reg for the split selects. No IO
or RVFI change.

Adapt to the lane ports. Keep the exact-result vectors for all
base and M ops through the wrapper `out`. Add checks that the mul_p
hi/lo halves match MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU for sign corner cases
(0x80000000, 0xffffffff, mixed signs).

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-002-r4s1 (regression, +14.04%): This used the same three cuts as its same-round sibling r4s0 (raw 64-bit DSP product registered into EX/MEM.mul_p behind a late_rd = mem_read | is_mul interlock, flat ID-selected ALU lanes, registered load byte-lane selects with load_data at the last forward level) and landed inside its own 90-95 MHz forecast (about 92.6 MHz if cycles match r4s0's 4.53M), but that is about 15% below r4s0's 106.5 MHz, a larger gap than r4s0's own ~9% place_option spread (97.7-106.5 MHz), so the plan itself is confirmed and the gap most likely comes from RTL detail inside the single-cycle EX -> ex_result -> forward loop (the visible candidate is r4s1's shift lane, a 33-bit SRA plus a separate SLL behind a shift_right mux), which is unverified without a timing report, so follow-ups should build on r4s0's RTL, not r4s1's.

title: Low-area zero-bubble decode predictor (JAL + BTFN-agree LUT-RAM table) that reuses ID's pc+imm adder, on the 80.6 MHz champion
motivation:
The champion (hyp-002-r3s1: 179.43 iter/s, 80.6 MHz, 4,491,817 cycles)
still pays one bubble for every taken branch, JAL and JALR. The Python
ISS count on the -O3 2K CoreMark ELF gives 295,904 taken branches,
49,629 JALs and 13,794 JALRs, i.e. 359k bubbles, about 8% of all
cycles.
hyp-003-r3s2 already showed that the prediction policy works. A
decode-time JAL + BTFN-agree 128x2-bit bimodal predictor cut cycles to
4,197,768 (-6.5%), matching the ISS forecast. It lost only because Fmax
fell 68.0 -> 59.1 MHz. Its worst path (regfile -> ALU -> alu_result)
contained no predictor logic. LESSONS points to placement pressure
from +385 LUT / +277 FF on a ~2.4k-LUT core with tied EX cones: a
256-flop counter table with a second read port, plus a dedicated
32-bit pc+imm adder.
Two things are different now:
  (1) The champion has no BSRAM regfile. Every EX cone starts at a
      plain flop, and the limiter is the EX ALU/MUL -> ex_result ->
      ID forward LUT -> ID/EX loop (7 cells, ~12.4 ns period). The
      predictor touches none of it.
  (2) In the merged IF/ID cycle, id_stage ALREADY computes
      pc_imm = pc + imm from the fetched word (imm_gen covers the B
      and J formats), for branch_target/AUIPC. That is exactly the
      predicted target, so no new adder is needed.
In the timed bench io_imemData is an LFSR flop, so the fetch-side
predictor path starts from a flop:
  flop -> imm_gen -> carry chain -> 2 mux LUTs -> PC
That is about 7-9 ns, well under the 12.4 ns period.
So the same -6.5% cycles can be bought for about a quarter of r3s2's
area. The table uses a handful of LUT-RAM slices, the pipeline carries
about 5 new FFs, and there is no second read port and no new adder.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict in the merged IF/ID cycle from the fetched instruction word and
verify only the DIRECTION in EX. The champion's kill mechanism
(redirect + flush_id kills exactly one slot) is unchanged, and RVFI
keeps reporting the resolved outcome.

1. Predictor (new rtl/branch_pred.sv, instantiated in core.sv or
   id_stage.sv). It reads the IF/ID bundle (raw imem word, pc):
     is_jal  = opcode == 1101111
     is_br   = opcode == 1100011 && funct3 not in {2,3}
     tgt_ok  = (is_jal ? instr[21] : instr[8]) == 0   // imm[1]==0, target aligned
     ctr     = tbl[pc[8:2]]          // 128 x 2-bit, async-read LUT-RAM
     dir_br  = instr[31] ^ ctr[1]    // agree-with-BTFN: ctr=0 => backward taken
     pred    = tgt_ok && (is_jal || (is_br && dir_br))
   The table is `logic [1:0] tbl [0:127]` with the
   syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram" attribute (same idiom as reg_file.sv),
   an initial zero fill, no reset and ONE sync write port. Correctness
   never depends on its contents, because EX checks every predicted
   direction, so an arbitrary or stale state only costs cycles. If
   Gowin will not infer it, use a 64-entry pc[7:2] table rather than
   flops.
2. if_stage next PC (the existing enable is unchanged):
     reset > redirect ? redirect_target
           : !stall   ? (pred ? pc_imm : pc + 4)
           : hold
   pc_imm is id_stage's EXISTING pc + imm (export it, or move the add
   into a shared spot). Do NOT add a second adder. Redirect stays at
   the last mux level. pred is decoded from the IF/ID bundle's instr
   (the same post-NOP-mux word that imm_gen/pc_imm already use), so it
   is automatically 0 on an imem-stall NOP slot. The PC holds on that
   cycle anyway. Keep the late EX redirect off the pred/pc_imm logic.
3. id_stage: latch pred (as pred_q) and ctr (2 bits) into ID/EX with
   the other data fields on !stall. flush and reset clear pred_q like
   the ctrl bits. Invariant: ID/EX captures a valid instruction only
   on a cycle when the PC also advanced using that same instruction's
   prediction. The capture enables are !stall_id && !flush_id versus
   !stall_if, and they differ only on an imem stall, when the slot is
   an invalid NOP with is_branch = is_jump = 0.
4. ex_stage redirect (direction-only check, same depth as today; pred_q
   is a flop folded into the existing is_branch/cond LUT):
     br_redir   = is_branch & (pred_q ? !branch_cond
                                      : branch_cond & !in.branch_target[1])
   (use the flop bit branch_target[1], not the cond-derived
    misalign_branch, so the compare -> redirect LUT gains no input depth)
     jal_redir  = is_jump & !is_jalr & !pred_q & !misalign_jump   // safety net
     jalr_redir = is_jalr & !misalign_jump                        // unchanged
     redirect   = br_redir | jal_redir | jalr_redir
     redirect_target = is_jalr ? {agu_sum[31:1],1'b0}
                     : (pred_q ? in.pre_result /* = pc+4 for branches */
                               : in.branch_target)
   The inner 2:1 mux has flop selects and flop data, so the late agu_sum
   still sees one LUT, as today. EX/MEM.pc_next, branch_taken, trap and
   reg_write all remain the RESOLVED outcome, so the RVFI and
   misalign-trap rules are untouched. A correctly predicted branch or
   JAL raises no redirect, so its target instruction (already in IF/ID)
   is kept. A predicted-taken branch that falls through redirects to
   pc+4 and flush_id kills the target slot.
5. Counter update is OFF the EX cone. EX/MEM carries ctr (2 FFs). The
   table write is driven from EX/MEM flops only:
     we    = EX/MEM.valid & ctrl.is_branch & !ctrl.is_illegal
     disag = EX/MEM.branch_taken ^ EX/MEM.instr[31]
     wdata = sat(ctr_q + (disag ? +1 : -1)),  waddr = EX/MEM.pc[8:2]
   While EX/MEM is held by a dmem stall, the same write repeats, which
   is idempotent. If a branch is in flight on the same index, IF reads
   a stale value; that is performance-only.
Area: about 40-80 LUT (32 PC-mux LUTs, decode, update, 8:1 table read
mux) plus 128x2 LUT-RAM and about 5 FF, against r3s2's +385 LUT and
+277 FF.
Expected cycles: about 4.20M, the r3s2 measurement of the identical
policy (-6.5%). If Fmax holds at 80-81 MHz, that gives about 192
iter/s (+7%). Fmax must stay within about 2% for the gain to clear
the 4.6% bar.
Implementation guards:
  - Check `make timing` and confirm the worst path is still the EX
    ALU/MUL loop, with no path through u_if/pc via imm_gen/pc_imm
    above ~11 ns.
  - Check LUT growth is under 100.
  - Check cosim cycles are around 4.20M (a sanity check that
    prediction fires).

changes.description: New module. Pre-decodes JAL and valid BRANCH from the IF/ID word and computes the target-alignment check (imm[1]==0). Holds a 128x2-bit agree-with-BTFN table in distributed LUT-RAM (async read at pc[8:2], one sync write port, zero initial value, no reset). Outputs pred and ctr. The write port takes waddr/wdata/we computed from EX/MEM flops.

Next-PC data mux becomes redirect ? redirect_target : (pred ? pc_imm : pc+4), with the enable unchanged (redirect || !stall). New inputs pred and pc_imm. No NOP or redirect changes on the IF/ID payload.
Export the existing pc_imm (pc + imm) for the IF next-PC mux, with no new adder. Latch pred_q and ctr[1:0] into ID/EX on !stall, and clear pred_q on flush/reset together with ctrl.
id_ex_t: add pred_q and ctr[1:0]. ex_mem_t: add ctr[1:0].

Direction-only verification: br_redir = is_branch & (pred_q ? !cond : cond & !misalign_branch); JAL redirects only if it was unpredicted and aligned; JALR is unchanged. redirect_target = is_jalr ? agu : (pred_q ? pre_result : branch_target). Pass ctr into EX/MEM. The pc_next, trap and reg_write semantics stay exactly as today (the resolved outcome).

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-003-r4s2 (regression, +5.60%): The low-area retry of r3s2's zero-bubble decode predictor (JAL + BTFN-agree 128x2 LUT-RAM counters with a single sync write port trained only from EX/MEM flops, IF's predicted next PC taken from id_stage's existing pc+imm adder, EX checking direction only with the redirect kept at the last next-PC mux level) scored 189.47 vs 179.43, close to its +7% forecast, which implies about 79.6 MHz (only ~1% below 80.6) if cycles fell to r3s2's ~4.20M, so it confirms that r3s2's -13% Fmax came from area/placement pressure and not from the prediction policy; it most likely lost only to sibling r4s0 (235.32 at ~106.5 MHz), and a rebase onto r4s0 must re-check timing first, because the fetch-side flop -> imm_gen -> pc+imm carry chain -> pred mux -> u_if/pc path was estimated at 7-9 ns, which is close to r4s0's ~9.4 ns period rather than safely under the old 12.4 ns.

title: Cut the three tied 10.2 ns cones: one-LUT branch resolve + registered PC select, 1-level ex_result merge (pre/div off the EX forward), no alu_b mux, EX-side MUL sign bits
motivation:
Fresh `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (hyp-20260929-001-r4s0,
235.32 iter/s, place_option 0 at 97.65 MHz; 5.33 ns clock insertion in
every arrival) shows three cones tied within 0.06 ns of data delay. They
fill the whole top 25:
  A. BRANCH -> PC, 10.205 ns (paths 1-6, 9-20, 22; 23-25 reach the
     ID/EX ctrl RESET pins at 10.085). rs2_val_0 -> 2.3 ns route ->
     31-cell compare carry chain (1.06 ns) -> 1.1 ns route -> SIX LUTs
     (u_if n328_s7/s6/s5/s3/s0 = branch_op case, taken, misalign,
     redirect | !stall, then pc_30_s3 at fanout 30) -> pc CE/D. The
     same redirect net drives flush_id -> ID/EX sync RESET.
  B. ALU LOOP, 10.159 ns (path 7; path 21 at 10.125 starts at
     ctrl.alu_src, i.e. the alu_b mux). rs1_val_29 -> shifter 2 LUT ->
     ex_result 4 LUT (the merge sum&sel_add | logic | sll | sr | slt |
     div&sel_div | pre&sel_pre has more than 10 inputs per bit) -> 2 ns
     route -> rs1_fwd -> ID/EX rs1_val.
  C. ADDER -> MUL SIGN, 10.154 ns (path 8). The sub flop (fanout 33)
     -> adder chain -> sum_31 -> 4 ex_result LUTs -> rs1_fwd_31 -> one
     extra LUT mul_a_sx = l_mul_sa & rs1_fwd[31] -> ID/EX.mul_a_sx.
LESSONS r2s0, r2s1 and r4s0 say tied cones must be cut together. Each
cone has 2-5 removable LUT levels, and every cut is cycle-neutral or costs
only a DIV-use bubble.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
A. Branch resolve ends one LUT6 (LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5/6 cluster) after the
   compare outputs. The PC D-mux leaves the redirect path.
   - ID decodes registered selects:
       br_ok  = BRANCH & !instr[8] (B-target 4-aligned; pc is always
                4-aligned)
       br_mag = BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU
       br_inv = BNE/BGE/BGEU
       br_u   = BLTU/BGEU
       br_mis = BRANCH & instr[8]
       jal_ok = JAL & !instr[21]
     They are cleared on flush like the other lane selects.
   - EX: eq = (rs1 == rs2). lt comes from ONE 33-bit borrow chain
     {~br_u & rs1[31], rs1} - {~br_u & rs2[31], rs2}; the old case
     builds up to three compare chains.
       cond      = (br_mag ? lt : eq) ^ br_inv
       br_taken  = br_ok & cond
       jalr_ok   = is_jalr & !(rs1[1] ^ imm[1] ^ (rs1[0] & imm[0]))
                   (flop-fed, off the chain)
       redirect  = br_taken | jal_ok | jalr_ok
     The misaligned-taken trap (br_mis & cond), branch_taken and pc_next
     only feed EX/MEM flops. EX exports cond's early terms to
     hazard_unit so that flush_id = (!dmem_stall & (load_use | jal_ok |
     jalr_ok)) | ((br_ok & !dmem_stall) & cond) has only lt/eq late.
   - IF: pc becomes seq_q/tgt_q/sel_q.
       cur_pc = sel_q ? tgt_q : seq_q    (imem_addr and IF/ID pc)
       tgt_q <= redirect_target          (every cycle, no enable)
       sel_q <= redirect
       seq_q <= stall_if ? cur_pc : cur_pc + 4   (independent of redirect)
     This equals the old pc(t+1) = redirect ? target : stall ? pc : pc+4
     exactly, including redirect-over-stall and a branch held in EX
     across a dmem stall. The redirect endpoint is one sel_q D pin instead
     of 32 pc CE/D pins at fanout 34. The new mux is flop -> LUT ->
     imem_addr (an LFSR XOR in the timed bench) / ID pc adders, all short.
B. ex_result becomes one LUT5 over pre-gated lanes.
   - Remove pre_result from ex_result. ID's forward splits
     sel?_ex into sel?_ex_alu = sel?_ex & !ID/EX.sel_pre, which takes
     ex_result at the last level, and sel?_ex_pre = sel?_ex & sel_pre,
     which takes the ID/EX.pre_result FLOP at the early level. Only select
     logic changes, so LUI+ADDI and AUIPC+ADDI pairs keep zero-bubble
     forwarding. JAL/JALR links are never EX-forwarded anyway because
     redirect squashes the next slot.
   - Remove div_result from ex_result. late_result = mem_read | mul | div,
     so a directly dependent op takes the existing one-cycle interlock
     (DIV is negligible in CoreMark). EX/MEM.alu_result D =
     ex_result | (sel_div & div_result) | (sel_pre & pre_result), which
     is one LUT5 after ex_result, the same depth as the forward path.
     MEM, WB, the regfile and RVFI are unchanged.
   - Fold sel_sll / sel_sr into the last shifter mux level, and lop is
     already a gated logic LUT. Per bit, ex_result = (sum & sel_add) |
     logic_g | sll_g | sr_g (| slt at bit 0): 5 inputs, one LUT5.
C. Remove the alu_b mux. For alu_src instructions other than stores
   (OP-IMM, LOAD, JALR, LUI/AUIPC), ID/EX.rs2_val captures imm instead of
   rs2. The select side absorbs it: sel2_ex/ld & !use_imm_b, and
   rs2_early = use_imm_b ? imm : (mem/wb/rf). EX feeds the ALU b
   straight from the rs2_val flop. Stores, branches, MUL and DIV still see
   raw rs2. The AGU keeps its own imm. For those use_imm_b instructions,
   ID/EX.rs2_addr is 0, so RVFI rs2_addr/rs2_rdata report "unused" (0/0)
   and the riscv-formal reg/insn checks stay exact.
D. MUL sign bits move to EX: a_sx = mul_sa_q & rs1_val[31] and
   b_sx = mul_sb_q & rs2_val[31]. That is one LUT in front of the DSP,
   whose output is the EX/MEM OREG with lots of slack. This takes
   mul_a_sx/mul_b_sx off the forward loop's tail. The ALTOPS and real
   multiplier branches both keep the same operand interface.
Expected: A falls to about 7-7.5 ns, B to about 8.2-8.5 ns and C to about
8 ns data. Fmax is then set by the next, unreported cone (the load extract
-> forward path was forecast at about 8.5-9 ns). The place-option median
goes from 106.5 to about 115-120 MHz with cycles within +0.1% (the DIV-use
bubble only). About +9-12% fitness. Area falls slightly: 2 compare chains
and 32 alu_b mux LUTs removed, 2 mul_sx flops dropped, about 34 PC flops
added.

changes.description: id_ex_t: add br_ok, br_mag, br_inv, br_u, br_mis, jal_ok, mul_sa, mul_sb; drop mul_a_sx/mul_b_sx. rs2_val doc: carries imm for non-store alu_src instructions.

Decode the registered branch selects and late_result |= is_div. Split the EX forward select into ex_alu (last level, ex_result) and ex_pre (early level, ID/EX.pre_result flop). Fold use_imm_b = alu_src & !mem_write into the rs2 selects and early mux (imm), zeroing rs2_addr for RVFI. Register mul_sa/mul_sb instead of the forwarded sign bits.

ALU b = rs2_val flop (no alu_src mux). ex_result = base lanes only; EX/MEM.alu_result D ORs in div/pre. eq + single 33-bit borrow chain, cond = (br_mag ? lt : eq) ^ br_inv, flop-fed jal_ok/jalr_ok, redirect = br_ok&cond | jal_ok | jalr_ok; misalign trap into EX/MEM only; export early flush terms + cond. MUL sign bits from rs1_val[31]/rs2_val[31].

title: Decoupled fetch: 2-entry IF->ID prefetch queue (bypassed) so imem stalls hide behind backend stalls, PC enable freed of hazard terms, redirect at the last PC mux level
motivation:
Fresh `make timing TARGET=bench` on the r4s0 champion (place_option 0,
97.65 MHz; the arrival times include 5.33 ns of clock insertion, data
delay ~10.2 ns) shows two cones tied within 0.05 ns:
  A. rs2_val -> 32-cell branch-compare carry chain (~1.1 ns) -> FIVE
     LUT levels in u_if (n328_s7/s6/s5/s3/s0, fanout 34) -> pc CE LUT
     (fanout 30) -> pc CE/D (paths 1-6, 9-20, 22), and the same
     redirect into the ID/EX ctrl RESET, which is flush_id (paths 23-25).
     Those five LUTs are the branch_op select, is_branch & cond,
     misalign kill, and `redirect || !stall_if`, where stall_if =
     load_use | imem_stall | dmem_stall | ex_busy.
  B. The single-cycle ALU loop: rs1_val -> shifter (2 LUT) ->
     ex_result AND-OR (4 LUT) -> ID forward LUT -> rs1_val (path 7,
     10.16 ns). The adder branch is tied at 10.13-10.15 ns (paths 8
     and 21: sub / alu_src -> alu_b mux -> carry -> ex_result ->
     forward -> mul_a_sx / rs1_val).
About 64% of each path is routing.
On the cycle side the largest single loss is fetch. imemReady is a
per-cycle ~22% random stall that is independent of the pipeline. Today
IF is lock-stepped with ID. Every backend stall cycle (dmem stall on
~22% of memory ops, load/mul-use bubble, divider) holds the PC and
refetches the same address, so a ready fetch slot is thrown away. Every
later imem-not-ready cycle then injects a NOP bubble. A fetch unit that
keeps fetching while the backend is stalled converts those wasted slots
into banked instructions that cover the next imem stall.
