hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two cycle-only changes that follow the fetch-structure timing rules
(flop-only write port, late control only on 1-bit valid flops, IF word /
flush_id / PC mux byte-identical):

(1) Re-key the fetch store so entry index K holds word(K+4). Write
word(A) at index (A-4)[11:2] = wprev[9:0] with tag (A-4)[19:12]. The
write port is still the PC flop -> decrement (already computed as wprev)
and imem_data under imem_ready. The read-side invariant keeps its form:
at PC p with v1_q = 1, DO = entry keyed p = word(p+4), and store_hit
still compares the stored tag with pc[19:12]. Sequential read index
becomes pc[11:2] + 1. On a predicted-taken advance the read index becomes
pc_imm[11:2], the low bits of id_stage's existing shared pc+imm adder,
with no extra adder:
  raddr = pred ? pc_imm[11:2] : pc[11:2] + 1
and then v1_q <= !redirect (pred no longer clears it). So at PC=T, DO
already holds word(T+4), and the T -> T+4 advance loads word_q/hit_q from
the store instead of imem. Redirect still clears v1_q and never reaches
the BSRAM address, because redirect is a tied ~9.1 ns cone.

The new mux path is IF word -> imm_gen -> low 10 carry bits -> 2:1 (pred)
-> BSRAM address register. The low bits finish early in the carry chain,
and pred is PC flop -> LUT-RAM -> one LUT, so the path is about 5-6 ns
against the 9.2 ns period. It only adds ~10 loads to pred and pc_imm[11:2],
whose critical endpoint is the high pre_result bits. Unlike r9s1, this is
one hard-BSRAM registered read port with one late select, not LUT-RAM
replicated per candidate PC feeding fabric flops.

(2) Let loop_buf CAPTURE use fetch-store hits. The word_q source select
becomes (rep_q || (cap_q && at_end_q)) ? mem[ridx] : store_word (all
flops). hit_q <= loop_back || (!pred && (rep_q ? !at_end_q : store_hit)).
The capture write becomes: enable cap_q && (hit_q || imem_ready), data
hit_q ? word_q : imem_data. Both are flop-only; this is exactly the IF
word when valid, and imem is read-only, so a hit word is the true word.
The capture-completion argument still holds, because the PC leaves an
address only when its word was valid (hit or imem_ready).

Expected: (1) removes the T+4 imem fetch after every predicted-taken
transfer outside replay, about 150-200k transfers x 0.28, or roughly 40-55k
cycles. (2) removes most imem stalls in capture passes, about 20-40k
cycles. Together that is about -2 to -3% of 3.547M cycles, with Fmax held
at ~109 MHz if nothing lands on the tied cones. This is below the 4.6% bar
on its own, so it is the round's low-risk micro_opt slot. The
implementation must run `make timing` before handoff and report bracketed
CoreMark cycles and median Fmax separately.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-001-r14s0 (regression, -2.66%): Re-keying r11s1's BSRAM fetch store so entry K holds word(K+4), with the read address raddr = pred ? pc_imm[11:2] : pc[11:2] + 1 so a predicted target's T+4 word is ready, plus fetch-store hits during loop_buf CAPTURE, scored 300.57 vs r11s1's 308.79 where +3% was forecast. No cycles or Fmax were reported, but fitness ≈ 10 × MHz / Mcycles implies about 103.4-104.5 MHz vs 109.53 at the forecast -2 to -3% cycles (106.6 MHz if no cycles were saved). The capture change is flop-only, so the most likely cause is the address mux: the IF word -> imm_gen -> pc+imm low bits -> pred-selected 2:1 path now ends at the BSRAM address and adds loads to both pred and the tied pc+imm cone. So r9s1's rule (an early-read fetch array takes its address from flops only) also holds for a single hard-BSRAM port with one late select, not just for replicated LUT-RAM reads. Both changes were in one build, so their shares cannot be split, and the loss is inside the ~4% placement spread. This is the third loss on the post-taken-transfer T/T+4 lever (after r12s0 and r12s2): any scheme that reaches the target's index before the target is in the PC flop needs IF-word-derived address bits, so the lever should stay closed.

title: 4-stage IF-ID-EX-WB: AGU in ID, dmem accessed in EX, zero-bubble load-use
motivation:
On the r11s1 champion (308.79, 109.53 MHz, 3,547,028 cycles, 2,922,016
retired instructions) the fetch side is now mostly hidden, and the ISS
count from r13s1 shows that the largest single stall source is the
load-use interlock: 203,959 true load-use pairs, i.e. 204k bubbles, or
5.75% of all cycles. About 136k of them are load -> branch pairs, which
two rounds (r13s0, r13s1) tried to recover by resolving the branch in MEM
and lost 11-13% Fmax, because they added a same-cycle redirect source to
the tied compare -> redirect -> PC/flush_id cone.
The bubble exists only because the load address is formed in EX, so the
dmem BSRAM is read one stage later than the ALU produces its result. If
the address is formed one stage earlier, in ID, the dmem read happens
in EX, and a load's data reaches the ID bypass at the same time as an ALU
result. Every load -> use pair (ALU, store data and branch consumers) then
issues back to back, with no new redirect source and no new compare.
The timed load path (address flop -> BSRAM DO -> load extract -> forward
LUT -> ID/EX) is the same cone as today; only its address flop moves from
EX/MEM to ID/EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the 5-stage pipeline into a 4-stage IF -> ID -> EX -> WB
pipeline in the "AGU-in-decode" style (as in the classic R3000/Pentium
AGI arrangement).

1. AGU moves into ID. For LOAD, STORE and JALR, id_stage computes
   agu = rs1_early + imm, where rs1_early is the non-EX part of the
   existing bypass (WB value or regfile LUT-RAM read). The sum is
   registered as ID/EX.mem_addr, which drives io_dmemAddr directly, so
   Gowin can still absorb it into the dmem BSRAM address register as it
   does with today's EX/MEM.mem_addr. Load byte-lane selects, the byte
   mask and the misalign check are decoded in ID from agu[1:0] (or in EX
   from the ID/EX flop bits, both flop-only) exactly as ex_stage does
   today.
   The adder never sees ex_result or load data, so the single-cycle
   ALU -> ex_result -> forward -> ID/EX loop does not get longer.
2. Address-generation interlock (AGI): if the IF word is a LOAD, STORE or
   JALR whose rs1 equals ID/EX.rd (reg_write, rd != 0), it waits one
   cycle, like today's load-use bubble. The next cycle the producer is in
   WB and its value arrives through the rs1_early WB source.
   hazard_unit's condition becomes
     late_q && (rd == rs1 || rd == rs2)  ||  wen_q && agi_op(IF) && rd == rs1
   and reuses the same rd == rs1 compare. late_result now means MUL* only
   (DIV stays behind ex_busy). A load -> load-address pair still bubbles
   once, the same as today. Store data (rs2) is not an AGI source and is
   forwarded normally.
3. dmem is accessed in EX. The load extract (mem_stage's flat byte-lane
   AND-OR, selects from ID/EX flops) runs on io_dmemRData in EX, and the
   result enters the ID bypass as part of the EX source:
     rs_fwd = sel_ex_alu ? ex_result : sel_ex_ld ? load_data : rs_early
   This is the same last-level shape as today's
   sel_ex ? ex_result : sel_ld ? mem_load_data : early. A dmem stall
   (!dmem_ready && ID/EX mem op, all flops) is handled exactly like
   ex_busy: IF and ID/EX hold, and EX/WB captures a bubble so WB drains.
   This reuses the existing divider stall structure, so EX/MEM no longer
   needs its own hold.
4. The MEM stage is deleted. EX/WB (the old MEM/WB) registers
   alu_result, the extracted load data, the 64-bit DSP product (no
   reset, on the EX/WB enable, as today) and every RVFI field. wb_stage
   picks load / ALU / product half for the regfile write and for the WB
   bypass source. The forward network drops from five sources (ex, ld,
   mem, wb, rf) to four (ex_alu, ex_ld, wb, rf), and the rs_early mux
   loses a level.
5. JALR takes its target from the ID/EX.mem_addr flop:
   redirect_target = is_jalr ? {mem_addr[31:1],0} : alt_target, and
   f_jr's misalign term is mem_addr[1]. Both become flop -> 1 LUT, which
   takes EX's rs1+imm carry chain off the redirect/PC cone. Branch
   resolve, the predictor, loop_buf, fetch_store, the IF word and the
   flush_id structure are otherwise unchanged. Predictor training moves
   from EX/MEM to EX/WB flops.

Cycle forecast, measured with the reference ISS (test/cosim/reference.py)
on the exact -O3 2K CoreMark build, bracketed by the MMIO markers:
2,922,015 instructions, 684,482 loads+stores, 203,959 load-use pairs
(matches r13s1). Of these, 135,320 are load -> branch and 59,270 are
load -> address (LOAD/STORE/JALR rs1), which still bubble. So
144,689 bubbles go away. The new AGI bubbles (a non-load producer
directly ahead of a LOAD/STORE/JALR base) number 66,975. MUL-use
(35,640) is unchanged. Net about -77.7k cycles, -2.2% (3.547M -> ~3.47M),
as a first-order count that ignores interactions with dmem stalls.
The implementer should confirm this in Verilator cosim and report
bracketed cycles and median Fmax separately.
At -2.2% cycles, clearing the 4.6% bar also needs Fmax to rise by
about 2.5% (~112 MHz). The case for that is the removed MEM stage (fewer
flops and forward LUTs, one less forward source on the tied loop) and the
carry chain taken off the JALR target. This is not guaranteed, because
r5s0, r6s0 and r8s0 showed that trimming levels alone rarely moves
Fmax on this core.
Fmax forecast: the load cone and the ALU loop keep their length, the
forward mux loses one input, the redirect-target path loses a carry
chain, and the MEM stage's ~150 flops and mux LUTs are removed, so area
goes down. The new ID AGU path (IF word -> LUT-RAM read -> WB/rf mux ->
32-bit carry -> BSRAM address) is parallel to today's IF word ->
imm_gen -> pc+imm -> pred -> PC path and must stay under it. The AGI
term adds one IF-word opcode decode on stall_if (a LUT input, not a
new level if folded with the rd compare). Expect 106-112 MHz.
Net: about +0 to +5% fitness (+2.2% from cycles alone at unchanged Fmax).

changes.description: Add the ID AGU (rs1_early + imm, sourced only from the WB value or the regfile read, never ex_result or load data), registered into ID/EX.mem_addr for LOAD/STORE/JALR together with the pre-decoded load byte-lane selects, byte mask and misalign flag. Split the EX forward source into sel_ex_alu / sel_ex_ld at the last mux level; drop the MEM source (rs_early = sel_wb ? wb_w_data : rf). late_result = MUL* only. Train-side ctr stays as is.
Three producers instead of four: ex (ID/EX; load or ALU, trap-cleared wen), wb (EX/WB), rf. Priority ex > wb > rf.

Replace the load-use term with MUL-use (late_q && rd==rs1|rs2) plus the AGI term (id_ex wen && IF word is LOAD/STORE/JALR && rd==rs1, rd!=0), sharing the rd==rs1 compare. dmem_stall = !dmem_ready && ID/EX mem op (flops) is handled like ex_busy: stall_if, hold ID/EX, and EX/WB captures a bubble. Delete stall_ex_mem/hold_mem_wb.

Drive io_dmemAddr/WData/WEn/REn from the ID/EX flops (mem_addr, rs2_val replicated, pre-decoded mask, misalign gate). Run the flat byte-lane load extract on io_dmemRData in EX and export load_data as the EX-load forward source. Remove the EX AGU. JALR target/misalign from ID/EX.mem_addr. The EX/WB register (the old MEM/WB payload incl. RVFI mem fields and the reset-free 64-bit DSP product register) is clocked here and captures a bubble (valid/reg_write clear) on ex_busy or dmem_stall.
Delete (its load extract, byte-lane replication, misalign trap and RVFI mem fields move into ex_stage/id_stage).
Select regfile write data from EX/WB: load data, alu_result, or the product half (sel_mul_lo/hi), which becomes the WB forward source.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-002-r14s1 (regression, -15.20%): Rebuilding the core as a 4-stage IF-ID-EX-WB pipeline with the AGU in ID scored 261.84 vs r11s1's 308.79, where +3% was forecast. No cycles or Fmax were reported, but fitness ≈ 10 × MHz / Mcycles implies about 91-93 MHz vs 109.53 (-15 to -17%) whether cycles fell by the ISS-forecast 2.2% or not at all, so the loss is Fmax. The build added two paths that start at the late IF word. The first is the ID AGU (IF word -> LUT-RAM regfile read -> WB/rf bypass mux -> 32-bit carry chain -> dmem BSRAM address): it is today's forward path plus a carry chain and a hard-block setup, not a peer of the pc+imm -> PC path. The second is an IF-word LOAD/STORE/JALR opcode decode on the load_use term that drives stall_if and flush_id, where r11s1's term uses only rs compares. Both were in one build, so their shares cannot be split. r13s0 and r13s1 also put an IF-word opcode term (BRANCH) on load_use and lost 11-13% with no ID adder, so that term, not only their same-cycle redirect, is a candidate common cause. Three builds have now lost 11-17% Fmax chasing a load-use interlock whose net recoverable share is only ~2-4% of cycles. The lever should stay closed unless a retry keeps every hazard term to IF-word rs compares, starts every new adder from flops, and reports cycles and median Fmax separately.

title: Predictor-speculated load->branch: drop the load->branch bubble, verify in MEM, registered 2-late redirect through the existing EX redirect net
motivation:
Measured data (r13s0/r13s1, Python ISS + Verilator on the exact CoreMark
build): 2,922,016 retired instructions, 203,959 load-use bubbles (5.75% of
the champion's 3,547,028 cycles), of which 135,320 have a conditional
BRANCH as the consumer (lbu -> beq/bne in core_state, list find/compare
loops, lw -> beqz). Both r13 builds removed that interlock and hit
3,417,583 cycles (-3.65%), so the prize is real and the predictor covers
those branches well: savings of 129.4k out of 135.3k bubbles imply only
~6k (~4.4%) late mispredicts. Both lost 11-13% Fmax because the late
compare drove a NEW SAME-CYCLE redirect with top priority on the PC mux,
flush_id and the loop_buf/fetch_store clears (r13s1 worst path:
rs2_val -> u_ex -> u_lsb -> u_if/pc). LESSONS explicitly asks for a retry
with a REGISTERED MEM resolve whose compare feeds only flops. Everything
else in the predictor category is <1.8% (51k direction mispredicts +
13.8k JALRs at 1 cycle each), so letting the existing predictor speculate
past load-dependent branches is the largest predictor lever left.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Let the decode-time predictor's guess stand for a BRANCH whose operand is
produced by the LOAD directly ahead of it (the pair the hazard unit
bubbles today), and verify it one stage late from flops only. The late
redirect enters the pipeline as an early FLOP term of the existing EX
redirect, so no new redirect source, PC-mux level or flush_id input is
added to the tied compare -> redirect -> PC/flush_id cone.

Timeline (L = load, B = dependent branch):
  t   : L in MEM, B in EX. B's EX redirect flags are cleared in ID (stale
        operand), so B never redirects in EX.
  t+1 : B in MEM, L in MEM/WB. Late compare in MEM from flops only:
        a = lsel1 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs1_val,
        b = lsel2 ? MEM/WB.read_data : EX/MEM.rs2_val,
        eq / lt / ltu (one subtractor + sign fix like alu_lanes) ANDed with
        B's carried one-hot "redirect-when" flags -> late_mis.
        late_mis feeds ONLY flop D inputs: late_q, tgt_q, and the gating of
        the ~5 side-effect bits of the EX/MEM capture of B+1
        (valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch) -> B+1 is a
        bubble in MEM, so dmem, forwarding and training never see it.
  t+2 : late_q=1: redirect = <existing flag&cmp OR tree> | late_q (late_q
        enters as an early term next to f_jal, not as an OR after the
        tree); redirect_target keeps its `is_jalr ? agu : alt` last-level
        shape with both inputs pre-muxed from flops
        (is_jalr_eff = is_jalr & !late_q, alt_eff = late_q ? tgt_q :
        alt_target). The existing flush_id / loop_buf / fetch_store /
        PC paths act on it unchanged. B+2 (in EX) is killed by gating the
        EX/MEM capture side-effect bits with the late_q flop; a DIV in B+2
        is cancelled by the existing flush (req drops -> IDLE).
A late mispredict costs 3 slots instead of the old 1 bubble + 1
mispredict, a correctly predicted late branch costs 0 instead of 1:
savings = 135.3k * (1 - 2*0.044) ~= 123k cycles -> ~3.42M cycles (-3.5%).

Cone discipline vs r13s0/r13s1:
  - no same-cycle redirect; late compare -> flops only.
  - no late_mis on flush_id, the PC mux select, loop_buf or fetch_store.
  - only loads are exempted (MUL -> branch keeps its interlock), so the
    exemption is `!(id_ex.ctrl.mem_read && if_is_br)` on load_use, with
    if_is_br the SAME legal-BRANCH decode branch_pred already builds;
    write it so it merges into the final load_use LUT (pre-combine the
    flop terms: id_ex is_mul vs is_load, rd != 0).
Correctness corner cases (all verified by formal/cosim):
  - L misaligned (trap, writes nothing): B must not use read_data. MEM
    detects late && MEM/WB L trapped (flop), forces late_mis with
    tgt = B.pc and clears B's MEM/WB.valid, i.e. B is replayed.
  - Chained late branches: late_mis is gated by EX/MEM.valid, and a
    killed slot's late bit is cleared with its valid.
  - Predictor training for B uses taken_late instead of the stale EX
    branch_taken (LUT-RAM write data only).
  - RVFI (pruned in synthesis): MEM/WB.rs1_val/rs2_val patched with the
    old MEM/WB.read_data when lsel; pc_next and is_illegal (taken to a
    misaligned target) recomputed from taken_late.
Area budget: ~+110-130 LUT (64 operand-select LUTs, 32-bit eq, one
33-bit subtract, flags), ~+75 FF (EX/MEM lf_*[6], lsel[2], late,
alt_target[32]; late_q, tgt_q[32]); no new LUT-RAM/BSRAM.
Expected: -3.5% cycles, Fmax within 0-2% of 109.5 MHz -> +1.5..+3.5%.
The implementer must run `make timing TARGET=bench` and report bracketed
cycles and median Fmax separately; if a new worst path runs through
late_q/tgt_q into u_if/pc or through if_is_br into load_use, move that
term to a pre-combined flop term before handoff.

title: Cycle-neutral endpoint trims: MUL sign bits built in EX from flops, and redirect confined to loop_buf's 1-bit mode flops
motivation:
The champion r11s1 (308.79, 109.53 MHz, 3.547M cycles) reports its worst
path as ID/EX.imm -> alu_b -> adder -> ex_result -> rs1_fwd[31] ->
ID/EX.mul_a_sx (12 levels, 37 cells). mul_a_sx = l_mul_sa && rs1_fwd[31]
(and mul_b_sx likewise) is one input MORE than the bit-31 forward LUT
already has (sel_ex, ex_result, sel_ld, load_data, rs_early = 5 inputs),
so these two flops sit one LUT past every other endpoint of the
single-cycle ALU -> forward loop. r8s0 and r13s0 also reported mul_b_sx
as their worst endpoint, so it is a recurring top endpoint, not noise.
In 9 of the last 12 builds the worst path was instead rs2_val -> compare
-> redirect -> u_lsb (cnt_q, end_q, cap_q, vld_q) or u_if/pc. loop_buf
gives redirect priority over its whole control block, so the redirect net
gates the enables of ~45 multi-bit state flops (end_q[29:0], start_q,
dist_q, cnt_q, at_end_q, full_q), even though only cap_q/rep_q/hit_q
have to react to it.
A cheaper-IPC micro-opt was ruled out first. An ISS trace model of
CoreMark (2.93M instructions, 2.21M fetches that are at least two
sequential steps past a taken transfer) shows that growing the BSRAM
fetch store from 1K to 4K words only removes 27.3k - 1.4k = ~26k conflict
misses (~7k stall cycles, 0.2%), so that geometry is already saturated.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two cycle-neutral cuts that shorten two recurring top endpoints without
adding any logic to the IF word, flush_id or the PC mux.
1. MUL extension bits leave the forward loop. id_stage no longer
   registers mul_a_sx/mul_b_sx from rs?_fwd[31]. It registers the decoded
   l_mul_sa/l_mul_sb instead (IF-word-only decode, not in the loop), and
   ex_stage forms a_sx = mul_sa_q & rs1_val[31] and b_sx = mul_sb_q &
   rs2_val[31] from ID/EX flops. That is one LUT in front of the DSP
   input, which has a whole cycle of slack (flop -> DSP -> mul_p_q
   register). The rs?_val[31] forward LUTs lose a load too.
2. Redirect acts only on loop_buf's 1-bit mode flops. cap_q and rep_q
   clear on redirect, and hit_q keeps its reset||redirect clear. All other
   loop_buf state (end_q, start_q, dist_q, cnt_q, at_end_q, full_q) is
   updated on !stall_if alone, by the same trig/rearm/loop_back/else
   priority as today, so redirect no longer feeds their enables. This is
   correct because that state is only read while cap_q||rep_q, or through
   rearm when full_q is set, and every entry into CAPTURE/REPLAY reloads
   cnt_q/at_end_q. A wrong-path trig in a redirect cycle only sets
   full_q = 0, which costs at most one missed rearm. A wrong-path
   loop_back can only set full_q when the capture has already written
   every word from start to end, and those are the true imem words
   (read-only), so a later rearm replays correct words.
fetch_store's v1_q already takes redirect as a 1-bit clear and is left
unchanged. Cycles should stay within +/-0.1% of 3.547M, and the gain has
to come from Fmax: removing the extra LUT on mul_*_sx lets the ALU loop
close at the rs?_val endpoints, and taking ~45 CE loads off the redirect
net shortens the compare -> redirect cone that dominates the sibling
reports. The forecast is capped by the next untouched cone (dmem DO ->
load_data -> forward, and imem_ready -> regfile address -> forward; the
r8s1 lesson), which is estimated about one LUT plus route (~0.4 ns)
behind, so the target is about 113-115 MHz. The implementer should
report bracketed cycles and median Fmax separately, and should also
check the post-synthesis worst-10 list to confirm that mul_*_sx and the
u_lsb enables left it.

The second limited redirect to clearing loop_buf's 1-bit cap_q/rep_q/hit_q, which took ~45 multi-bit clock-enable loads off the compare -> redirect net. No cycles or Fmax were reported, but at the unchanged 3.547M cycles the design intended, the score implies about 110.4 vs 109.53 MHz: ~0.07 ns recovered against a forecast of 0.3-0.4 ns. title: Posted stores: 1-entry store buffer so a STORE never freezes the pipeline on dmem backpressure (flop-only stall terms, D-side address mux)
motivation:
r11s1 (308.79, 109.53 MHz, 3.547M cycles) hid nearly all imem
backpressure, so the largest stall source left that has not been
closed is dmem backpressure (~5-7% of cycles: every LOAD/STORE in MEM
waits p/(1-p) ~= 0.28 cycles at 22% stalls, and the whole pipeline
freezes). r12s1 showed loads cannot be helped without a RAM read and
compare on the global dmem_stall net. Stores are different: nothing
downstream consumes a store's result, so a store can retire as soon as
it is captured and be written to dmem later, in the first bus-ready
cycle. No store buffer / posted-store build has been tried on this core
(log mentions "posted stores" only as an untried small lever).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 1-entry posted-store buffer (sb_v, sb_addr[31:0], sb_wdata[31:0],
sb_wen[3:0]) in mem_stage and change the dmem_stall rule so that a
STORE in MEM never stalls unless the buffer is already full:

1. Policy (all inputs are flops: EX/MEM ctrl, sb_v, io_dmemReady):
     store_in_mem = EX/MEM.mem_write (not misaligned)
     load_in_mem  = EX/MEM.mem_read
     dmem_stall   = load_in_mem  && (!dmem_ready || sb_v)
                 || store_in_mem && sb_v && !dmem_ready
   A store in MEM with an empty buffer always completes: it writes
   directly when ready, else it is posted into the buffer and retires
   normally (RVFI mem_* fields unchanged, taken from EX/MEM as today).
   A store with a full buffer and ready=1 drains the buffer this cycle
   and posts itself (sb <= new store). A load waits while the buffer is
   full (drain first), which makes load-after-store ordering exact
   without any address compare (no RAW forwarding, no compare on the
   stall net). dmem_stall stays one LUT on flops, as today (it gains
   only the sb_v flop input), per the r12s1 lesson.

2. Bus drive: the bench maps dmem to BSRAM by absorbing the flop that
   drives io_dmemAddr (r2s0 lesson), so no mux may sit between that
   flop and the port. Keep io_dmemAddr / io_dmemWData / io_dmemWEn /
   io_dmemREn each driven directly by a flop: add bus_addr_q,
   bus_wdata_q, bus_wen_q, bus_ren_q whose D inputs select, on the
   existing EX/MEM enable, between the next EX/MEM memory op (agu_sum,
   rs2 replicated, byte mask precomputed in EX from agu_sum[1:0]/width)
   and the buffer contents when the buffer will be draining next cycle
   (sb_v_next && !next is a load/store that owns the bus). The select
   is built only from flops and EX-stage decode flops (ID/EX ctrl), so
   the only new logic on the AGU -> address path is one 2:1 LUT after
   the carry chain; if `make timing` shows that path within 3% of the
   worst path, instead keep EX/MEM.mem_addr as the port flop and
   drain the buffer only in cycles where EX/MEM holds a non-memory op
   (the drain then writes sb_addr through a registered path loaded one
   cycle ahead from flops).

3. Drain: while sb_v and the bus is not owned by a MEM-stage op, the
   buffer presents its write; sb_v clears on the first cycle with
   io_dmemReady = 1. Loads are the only ops that wait for it.

Expected cycles: stores are roughly a third of CoreMark's memory ops,
so ~2-2.5% of cycles are store backpressure; minus the extra
drain-before-load waits, forecast -1.5 to -2.5% cycles. Fabric cost
~+70 FF / +40 LUT, no new late net (IF word, flush_id, redirect/PC
mux, forward network untouched). Report cycles, store-stall cycles
saved and median Fmax separately.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-002-r15s1 (regression, -8.25%): A 1-entry posted-store buffer scored 283.31 vs r11s1's 308.79 where +2% was forecast. It let a STORE retire under !dmem_ready (dmem_stall = load && (!ready || sb_v) || store && sb_v && !ready) and drove the dmem pins from new bus port flops. Each port flop's D input picks between the EX request (agu_sum, replicated rs2, and an EX-built byte mask) and the buffer contents. No cycles or Fmax were reported, but fitness ≈ 10 × MHz / Mcycles implies about 98-100.5 MHz vs 109.53, whether cycles fell by the forecast 1.5-2.5% or not at all. Holding Fmax would need ~3.87M cycles (+9%), and the drain-before-load rule only moves a posted store's wait onto the next load, so the loss is Fmax: ~0.8-1.1 ns, about one LUT plus routing. The most likely cause is the buffer/AGU 2:1 select after the 32-bit carry chain, on the D input of io_dmemAddr's flop. Gowin pulls that flop into the dmem BSRAM address register (r2s0), so the path ends at a hard-block setup, and the select also comes from sb_v, dmem_ready and the stall. So the agu_sum -> dmem-address path was within about one LUT of the critical path, and the report shows no sign that the spec's `make timing` gate on it ran. This is r14s0's rule on the data side: a BSRAM port's address flop should take the raw adder output with no select after it. A drain on the single dmem port always needs a second address source, and the whole prize is ~2% of cycles, so posted stores should stay closed unless a per-endpoint timing report first shows more than one LUT of slack on agu_sum -> dmem address.

title: Predictor-speculated load->branch, retried with a flop-predecoded is-branch bit, loop_buf end_q moved off the late redirect/stall/pred nets, MUL sign bits built in EX
motivation:
Measured numbers from the champion r11s1 and the ISS: 308.79 at 109.53 MHz median
(seeds 108.2/109.5/109.5), 3,547,028 cycles, 2,922,016 retired instructions, so about
625k overhead cycles. The largest overhead is the load-use interlock (204k bubbles).
135k of those are LOAD -> BRANCH pairs, which the direction predictor can speculate past.
The branch predictor itself has almost nothing left: ~51k direction mispredicts plus
~14k JALRs, under 2% of cycles even with perfect prediction. So load->branch speculation
is the largest lever left in the predictor category.

r14s2 did that speculation with a registered late verify and measured 3,423,469 cycles
(-3.5%). But it lost Fmax: 101.99 MHz (seeds 100.5/102.0/102.0) vs 109.53. Its reported
worst path was
  cpu/u_id/reg_q.rs2_val_0 -> u_ex (compare -> redirect) -> u_if -> cpu/u_lsb/end_q_23
at 15.243 ns. r14s0 had the same kind of endpoint, rs2_val_0 -> ... -> u_lsb/end_q_0, at
16.069 ns. So the limiter was not the new MEM compare. It was loop_buf's 30-bit end_q
register, whose clock enable is the priority chain
  !reset && !redirect && !stall_if && !loop_back && !rearm && trig.
That chain puts redirect (the EX compare), stall_if (IF word -> load_use) and
trig/pred (IF word -> branch_pred LUT-RAM) on 30 CE loads. r14s2 made stall_if later by
adding an IF-word BRANCH-opcode decode to the load_use exemption, so this chain became
the worst path. LESSONS asks for exactly this retry: take the is-branch bit from a flop
and keep load_use to IF-word rs compares.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild r14s2's load->branch speculation on r11s1, removing both suspected Fmax costs,
and add one small cut on the champion's own worst endpoint.

1. Speculate past LOAD -> BRANCH (same policy as r14s2). If the IF word is a legal
   BRANCH and its only late-result hazard is a LOAD in ID/EX, it is not bubbled. It
   enters EX with a "late" tag (which operand, or both, comes from the load). ID clears
   its f_* redirect-when flags, so EX never redirects on the stale operand. The
   prediction made at decode time stands. In MEM, the branch recomputes eq/lt/ltu from
   flops only: MEM/WB.read_data for the loaded operand and EX/MEM.rs?_val for the
   other. The branch carries the registered f_* flags (as g_* bits) and its alt_target.
   That compare feeds only flop D inputs: late_q and tgt_q. One cycle later, late_q is
   an early OR term on the existing EX redirect, and tgt_q is pre-muxed into
   redirect_target with a flop select. No new redirect source and no PC-mux level is
   added. When late_q fires, the younger slots in EX/MEM and ID/EX are killed through
   valid, reg_write, mem_read/mem_write and the fwd enable. The dmem write enable is
   gated by late_q, a flop. A mispredicted late branch costs 3 slots instead of
   today's bubble plus 1. EX/MEM.pc_next and branch_taken for RVFI, and predictor
   training, take the MEM-resolved outcome for late branches. MUL -> branch keeps the
   interlock.

2. The is-branch bit comes from flops, not from the IF word:
     br_if = hit_q ? word_br_q : (imem_ready && imem_br)
   imem_br is a 2-LUT decode of the io_imemData flop (opcode 1100011, funct3[2:1]
   != 01). It runs in parallel with the IF-word LUT, not behind it. word_br_q is a
   predecode bit written next to every stored word. loop_buf's LUT-RAM grows from
   16x32 to 16x33, and fetch_store's BSRAM entry grows from 41 to 42 bits, both
   written from decode(imem_data) under the existing flop-only write enables. It is
   loaded into a 1-bit register beside word_q, from the same unconditional source
   select. The load_use term stays: late_result && rd != 0 && (rd == rs1 || rd == rs2)
   from the IF-word rs fields, ANDed with !(br_if && ID/EX.is_load). The exemption term
   arrives no later than the rs compares.

3. end_q gets a flop-only enable. Every time CAPTURE sits on its loop branch (cap_q &&
   at_end_q, both flops), end_q <= pc[31:2]. By the loop_buf invariant
   pc == start + 4*(dist - cnt), that pc is the trigger branch. full_q is set only by
   loop_back, which happens on that same edge. cap_q = 1 implies full_q = 0, and every
   trig that is not a rearm clears full_q. So full_q = 1 still implies that end_q is the
   held loop's branch, and the rearm compare is exact, with the same cycle count. This
   removes redirect, stall_if, trig and pred from 30 CE loads, which was the worst
   endpoint in r14s0 and r14s2. Only full_q, cap_q, rep_q, cnt_q, dist_q, start_q and
   at_end_q keep the late chain.

4. MUL sign bits are built in EX. The champion's worst path ends at
   u_id/reg_q.mul_a_sx: imm -> ALU -> ex_result -> rs1_fwd[31] -> AND l_mul_sa ->
   mul_a_sx, at 14.534 ns arrival. Register the decoded l_mul_sa/l_mul_sb in ID/EX
   instead, and form a_sx = mul_sa_q & rs1_val[31] in front of the DSP, which feeds
   only the DSP operand and product register. This removes one LUT from that endpoint,
   and ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val become the loop's endpoints, as in r5s0/r6s0.

Forecast. Cycles: r14s2 measured 3.423M, so -3.5%. Fmax: 109.5 MHz held if items 2-3
remove r14s2's worst cone and item 4 gives ~0-2%. Net about +3 to +6%, centered near
+4.5%. If Fmax falls below ~107 MHz again, the load->branch lever should be treated as
closed. Report cycles and median Fmax separately, and before handoff run `make timing`
to confirm that end_q and mul_a_sx are no longer endpoints.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-003-r15s2 (regression, -9.91%): This build rebuilt r14s2's load -> branch speculation on r11s1 (flop-only MEM compare, late_q/tgt_q folded into the EX redirect) with both of r14s2's suspected Fmax costs removed. The cost lies in the late-resolve machinery that all four load -> branch builds share. Candidates are the late_q ? tgt_q level ahead of the redirect_target -> PC mux, the late-mispredict kill terms on the EX/MEM and ID/EX D inputs, ID's late tags that clear the f_* flags from the IF-word rs compares, and the added area. The 6.6% gap to r14s2 is beyond the ~4% placement spread, so the predecode plumbing may have added cost of its own. The result is far below the forecast's own 107 MHz kill threshold, and five interlock builds have now lost 3.5-17% Fmax for a ~3.5% cycle prize, so load -> branch speculation should stay closed.
